metadata.title: The Harvest
metadata.description: You wake in a stasis pod aboard a massive alien vessel. The Choir — eyeless bio-mechanical drones — are harvesters serving an ancient intelligence called The Convergence that consumes planets. Your pod malfunctioned. You're loose on a ship full of things that want you back in the jar. Below, a planet is being consumed alive.
metadata.author: ai-generated

setting.ambient_text: A subsonic hum vibrates through your bones. Amber fluid drains from your cracked pod, pooling on the organic-metallic floor. Bioluminescent veins pulse in the walls. Somewhere, something clicks — precise, mechanical, patient.

items.name: Stasis Fluid Vial
items.description: A vial of amber stasis fluid from your broken pod. The liquid shimmers faintly, still biologically active.

then.text: The fluid is warm and viscous, with a faint amber glow. It preserved you — and hundreds of other specimens — in suspended animation. The biochemistry is alien but clearly designed to sustain organic life.
You swirl the vial gently. The fluid moves like honey, clinging to the glass. Something about it feels... alive.

items.name: Pod Glass Shard
items.description: A curved shard from your broken stasis pod. Sharp enough to cut.

then.text: Translucent and curved, still faintly stained with amber fluid. The edges are razor-sharp. Not glass exactly — some alien composite that's stronger and lighter.
You test the edge against your thumb. It draws blood immediately. Careful with this.

items.name: Surgical Probe
items.description: An alien surgical instrument — curved bone-like material with a fine tip.

then.text: It looks grown rather than manufactured — smooth bone-like material tapering to a needle-fine point. The handle has organic ridges shaped for fingers much longer than yours. But it fits well enough in your small hands.

items.name: Containment Key Card
items.description: A bio-organic access card pulled from the security hub. Pulses faintly with stored energy.

then.text: Not plastic — something closer to compressed cartilage, embedded with bioluminescent circuits. It pulses like a heartbeat. Keyed to the containment deck's security systems.

items.name: Data Crystal — Personal Log
items.description: A small crystalline data storage device from the specimen archive. Contains a Choir officer's personal records.

then.text: The crystal is the size of your thumb, faceted, with internal light patterns that shift when you tilt it. A Choir personal log — and embedded in the data structure, fragments of a translation cipher. This is piece one of four.

items.name: Nutrient Paste Tube
items.description: A tube of grey nutrient slurry from the feeding station. Smells like wet cardboard and ozone.

then.text: Standard specimen feed. The tube is soft, organic material. The paste inside is grey, odorless, nutritionally complete for a dozen different species. Edible but unappetizing. Could also be used as bait — the drones are programmed to retrieve spilled feed.

items.name: Specimen Tag
items.description: Your own specimen identification tag from the stasis pod. Proof of what you are to them.

then.text: A small organic tag, pulled from your pod's label slot. Alien script — you can't read it yet — but it's your entry in their collection. Proof that you were catalogued. Proof that you exist as something more than a specimen.

items.name: Emergency Suit Helmet
items.description: An alien emergency space helmet. Too large for you, but still functional.

then.text: Designed for a Choir skull — far too large for you, but the visor seals automatically when worn. The internal atmosphere system still works. It would protect you from vacuum or toxic environments, even if it sits like a fishbowl on your shoulders.

items.name: Ventilation Map
items.description: Scratches in the vent shaft walls that form a crude map. You traced them onto a flat surface.

then.text: Someone — or something — scratched a map of the ventilation system into the shaft walls. Previous escape attempts. The map shows branching paths between containment sections, and marks dead ends with deep gouges. One path leads to the operational decks.

items.name: Severed Neural Tendril
items.description: A section of neural interface tendril, severed from a Choir dormancy alcove.

then.text: Rubbery, organic, about a foot long. The cut end still sparks faintly with bio-electric impulses. The Choir use these to interface with their ship's systems. With the right adapter, you could too — if you could trick it into accepting non-Choir biology.

items.name: Ship's Black Box
items.description: The Choir vessel's flight recorder. Contains the complete mission log — including records of every world consumed.

then.text: A dense, heavily shielded data device. It contains everything: navigation logs, mission parameters, specimen records, and communications with The Convergence. This is proof of what they've done — and what they're doing to the planet below.

items.name: Power Cell
items.description: A Choir power cell from engineering. Compact, immensely powerful, warm to the touch.

then.text: Bio-organic casing around a dense energy core. It hums faintly and radiates warmth. A single cell powers a Choir shuttle for weeks. Handle with care — damage to the casing would release the stored energy violently.

items.name: Resonance Disruptor
items.description: A Choir tool repurposed as a weapon. Emits a subsonic pulse that disrupts bio-mechanical systems.

then.text: Not a weapon by design — it's a maintenance tool for recalibrating Choir mechanisms. But aimed at a bio-organic lock, it scrambles the resonance patterns. Aimed at a drone, it disrupts motor functions for a few seconds. In your hands, it's the closest thing to a universal key.

items.name: Navigation Chip
items.description: A crystalline navigation module from the bridge. Contains star charts and jump coordinates.

then.text: A slim crystal wafer etched with navigation data. Star charts, jump coordinates, the Convergence's mapped path across galaxies. Without this, no ship leaves this system — the jump points are too complex to calculate manually.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 2
items.description: A data pattern extracted from the Choir's resonance chamber. The second piece of the translation key.

then.text: Extracted from the communal resonance patterns in the Choir's living quarters. Their 'language' is subsonic vibration, and this fragment maps vibration patterns to meaning. Combined with the other fragments, it could let you read all alien text.

items.name: Choir Resonance Crystal
items.description: A crystal from the ship's data core that resonates at the Choir's communication frequency.

then.text: Deep purple, perfectly smooth, vibrating at a frequency you can feel in your teeth. It's tuned to the Choir's subsonic communication band — a piece of their network made solid. The same resonance frequency the Convergence uses to control its harvesters.

items.name: Bio-Garden Extract
items.description: A concentrated extract from the ship's hydroponics bay. Bioluminescent, biochemically complex.

then.text: Harvested from the alien plants in the bio-garden. The extract glows faintly blue-green and contains an extraordinary density of biological compounds. The Choir uses it for everything from nutrition to neural repair. In the right combination, it could interface organic with crystalline systems.

items.name: Comm Array Schematics
items.description: Technical diagrams of the ship's communication array. Details frequencies, power requirements, and range.

then.text: Detailed schematics showing the communications array's architecture. Frequency ranges, power routing, targeting systems. With these, the array on the planet's nexus could be recalibrated to broadcast across the galaxy — if you could reach it.

items.name: Shuttle Fuel Line
items.description: A replacement fuel conduit for the damaged shuttle. Organic tubing with self-sealing connectors.

then.text: Bio-organic tubing that carries fuel from the bay's supply to the shuttle's engines. The connectors seal automatically when pressed into place. You'll need this, plus a power cell, to get the damaged shuttle flight-ready.

items.name: Drone Antenna
items.description: A sensory antenna pulled from a disabled maintenance drone. Still picks up Choir signals.

then.text: A thin, segmented antenna that twitches faintly in your hand — it's still receiving signals. It picks up the subsonic frequencies the Choir use to coordinate. Holding it near your ear, you can hear distant clicks and hums. An early warning system.

items.name: Coolant Flask
items.description: A sealed flask of reactor coolant from engineering. Extremely cold, mildly corrosive.

then.text: The flask is frosted on the outside — the coolant inside is near absolute zero. A crack in the seal would release a burst of freezing vapor. Useful for cooling overheated systems, or as an emergency weapon against anything organic.

items.name: Bio-Garden Fiber
items.description: Strong, flexible fiber harvested from alien plants. Tougher than any natural rope.

then.text: Harvested from the tendrils of the hydroponics plants. Incredibly strong and flexible — the Choir use it in construction and repair. It can be woven, tied, or wrapped. Combined with something sharp, it would make an excellent handle or binding.

items.name: Shuttle Emergency Beacon
items.description: A distress beacon from the crashed shuttle. Can recall any shuttle within signal range.

then.text: A compact transmitter designed to recall a shuttle to its beacon location. The signal range covers the entire planet. If there's a working shuttle in orbit or on the surface, this will bring it to you. Your ticket off this rock — if you choose to leave.

items.name: Wasteland Mineral Sample
items.description: Crystalline mineral from the base of a siphon tower. Infused with residual Convergence energy.

then.text: The soil near the siphon towers has been transformed — crystallized by the Convergence's energy extraction. This sample still holds a faint charge, a dampened echo of the energy that flows through the towers. It resists energy flow rather than conducting it.

items.name: Siphon Crystal Fragment
items.description: A fragment broken from an energy siphon tower. Pulses with raw Convergence energy.

then.text: It burns cold in your hand and crackles with contained energy. A piece of the Convergence's harvesting infrastructure, still charged with stolen planetary life force. Incredibly dangerous. Incredibly powerful. A key component for anything that needs to interact with Convergence energy systems.

items.name: Refugee Journal
items.description: A personal journal from the refugee camp. Written by a four-armed scientist in the final days.

then.text: The journal of Dr. Kaelith, a physicist who fled the city when the siphons began. Entries detail the final days — the panic, the failed defenses, the evacuation that came too late. Embedded in the margins: notation patterns that match the translation cipher format. Fragment three of four.

items.name: Fungal Extract
items.description: A concentrated extract from the bioluminescent fungi in the grove. Glows purple in the dark.

then.text: The fungi survived the Convergence's harvesting — they feed on the residual energy rather than being drained by it. The extract has remarkable properties: it promotes healing in organic tissue and, combined with the right compounds, can suppress neural detection.

items.name: Echo Stabilizer
items.description: Military-grade alien technology from the bunker. Stabilizes the energy field around Echoes, making them safe to approach.

then.text: A handheld device that projects a stabilization field. The planet's military developed it to study the Echoes — remnants of their people trapped in the Convergence's energy. It calms the chaotic energy patterns, making Echoes coherent enough to interact with safely. Without it, getting close to an Echo is like standing in a lightning storm.

items.name: Alien Sidearm
items.description: A four-armed species' personal weapon. Energy-based, partially charged.

then.text: Designed for a four-armed grip — you need both hands to hold it steady. The energy cell is partially depleted: maybe six shots. Each shot is devastatingly loud. Use it wisely, or not at all.

items.name: Bunker Defense Schematics
items.description: Military blueprints showing the planet's defense strategy against the Convergence.

then.text: Detailed military plans for the planet's last stand. Orbital defense satellite positions, ground-based weapon emplacements, and — most importantly — partial schematics for a weapon designed to disrupt the Convergence's energy systems. The plans are incomplete, but they confirm the weapon was built.

items.name: Survival Rations
items.description: Preserved alien food from the refugee camp. Still sealed, still edible.

then.text: Vacuum-sealed packages of concentrated nutrition. The labels show a four-armed figure eating contentedly. Not designed for your biology, but close enough. Eating one restores energy and clears your head.

items.name: Signal Flare
items.description: An emergency signal flare from the crashed shuttle. Burns bright, burns loud.

then.text: A human-made signal flare from the Outrider's emergency kit. Pull the cap and it burns blinding white for thirty seconds. Useful as a signal, a light source, a distraction, or — wrapped with the right material — an improvised torch.

items.name: Climbing Pitons
items.description: Metal spikes from the refugee camp's supplies. Designed for climbing rocky terrain.

then.text: Alien-made climbing aids — hardened metal spikes with looped heads for roping. The refugees used them to navigate the wasteland's shattered terrain. Essential for vertical surfaces your small stature can't otherwise reach.

items.name: Radiation Badge
items.description: A sensor badge from the bunker. Changes color in the presence of dangerous Convergence energy.

then.text: A simple but effective device — the crystalline strip changes color from green (safe) to yellow (caution) to red (lethal). The planet's military used them to navigate near siphon towers and Convergence infrastructure. Near the nexus, it'll be essential for finding safe paths.

items.name: City Keystone
items.description: An ornamental keystone from the grand plaza's central statue. Opens restricted areas throughout the city.

then.text: A crystalline key shaped like a miniature four-armed figure. It was built into the plaza's central statue — a city administrator's master key. It interfaces with the city's door systems, granting access to government buildings, the war room, and restricted infrastructure.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 4
items.description: The final fragment of the translation cipher, found in the city's library.

then.text: The library's master index contained the final cipher fragment — a Rosetta stone the city's linguists compiled to communicate with the Choir during failed negotiations. With all four fragments, you can read every piece of alien text in the game.

items.name: Weapon Core
items.description: The heart of the civilization's countermeasure weapon. A dense crystalline sphere pulsing with contained energy.

then.text: Heavy for its size — it feels like holding a small star. The weapon core was designed to resonate at the Convergence's own frequency, turning its stolen energy back on itself. Alone it's inert. Combined with the right components, it becomes the key to destroying the nexus.

items.name: Defense Grid Controller
items.description: A command module for the planet's orbital defense satellite network.

then.text: The planet's last line of defense — a controller for orbital weapons satellites. Most satellites are destroyed, but a few remain dormant in orbit. With enough power, they could be reactivated for one devastating strike.

items.name: Alien Personal Locket
items.description: A delicate locket from a residential home. Contains a holographic family portrait.

then.text: A small crystalline locket on a chain. Inside: a holographic portrait of a four-armed family — two adults, three children, all smiling. The youngest is holding a toy that looks like a simplified version of the siphon towers. They had no idea what was coming. Carrying this near coherent Echoes triggers powerful reactions.

items.name: Power Cell Adapter
items.description: An adapter that bridges the planet's technology with alien power sources.

then.text: The city's engineers designed this to interface their technology with captured Choir power cells. It converts between bio-organic energy formats and the civilization's crystalline power systems. A universal translator for alien technology.

items.name: Prophet's Crystal
items.description: A sacred crystal from the temple. Shows visions of possible futures when held.

then.text: The temple's priests used crystals like this for divination — and they were right more often than chance allows. Holding it, you see flashes: a nexus in flames. A signal reaching distant stars. A crystalline intelligence, afraid. A small creature, choosing. The visions are fragmented but feel profoundly real.

items.name: Railway Pass Token
items.description: An access token for the city's underground transit system.

then.text: A small crystalline disc — a transit pass. The underground railway still has power in some sections. This token activates the rail cars, allowing fast travel between the city's districts. The tunnels also connect to deeper passages beneath the city.

items.name: Resonance Tuning Fork
items.description: A ceremonial tuning fork from the temple. Vibrates at the frequency of the former civilization's communication.

then.text: The four-armed species communed through vibration, like the Choir but natural. This tuning fork produces their base resonance frequency. Combined with the Echo Stabilizer, it could enable full two-way communication with coherent Echoes — letting you truly speak with the dead.

items.name: Lab Safety Goggles
items.description: Protective eyewear from the research lab. Filters dangerous energy wavelengths.

then.text: Oversized for your face but functional. The lenses filter the blinding energy wavelengths produced by Convergence systems. The researchers wore these when studying siphon tower samples. Essential for looking directly at high-energy areas without going blind.

items.name: Ancient Blueprint
items.description: Complete assembly instructions for the countermeasure weapon. Found in the research lab.

then.text: A holographic blueprint showing the complete countermeasure weapon assembly. Three components: a primed weapon core, an energy dampener, and a siphon crystal fragment. The assembly order is critical — wrong sequence damages the core. Core first, dampener second, crystal last.

items.name: Convergence Energy Sample
items.description: Pure Convergence energy contained in a crystalline vial. Incredibly dangerous.

then.text: The vial is cold enough to burn and bright enough to read by. Inside: pure harvested planetary energy — the lifeforce of an entire world, concentrated. The crystal containment barely holds it. This is what the Convergence feeds on. This is what it's stealing.

items.name: Ancient Access Key
items.description: A key from the Convergence's stasis gallery. Opens the deepest sections of the nexus.

then.text: Not Choir-made. Not from the planet's civilization. This key predates both — it belongs to the Convergence itself, or whatever built the original nexus infrastructure. A crystalline fractal pattern that interfaces with the oldest locks in the structure.

items.name: Curator's Signal Device
items.description: The Curator's personal communication device. Can call the Choir vessel from orbit.

then.text: Taken from — or given by — the Curator itself. This device is keyed to the Curator's authority aboard the Choir vessel. It can recall the ship, issue commands to drones, and override security protocols. In friendly hands, it's a powerful ally. In desperate hands, it's a weapon.

items.name: Core Interface Module
items.description: A module from the control spire that allows direct neural interface with the Convergence intelligence.

then.text: The Choir use these to receive instructions from the Convergence. It translates crystalline energy patterns into neural signals and vice versa. It wasn't designed for non-Choir biology, but with the right biochemical preparation, it could bridge any mind to the Convergence. The question is whether you'd come back.

items.name: Escape Shaft Key
items.description: A mechanical key that opens the former civilization's emergency escape shaft in the nexus.

then.text: Found in the weapon assembly area — the former civilization's staging ground for their assault on the nexus. This key opens the emergency shaft they carved as an exit route. The shaft leads up and out, to the planet's surface. Your way out, if you choose to take it.

combinations.message: You wrap the bio-fiber tightly around the base of the glass shard, creating a secure grip. The alien fiber bonds to the glass — stronger than tape, flexible as leather. A proper blade now.

You mix the nutrient paste with the stasis fluid. The combination reacts — the paste absorbs the fluid and turns a deep amber. The stasis biochemistry that kept you unconscious for days is now concentrated in a smearable compound. Touch it and sleep.

You pulse the disruptor through the key card's bio-circuits, overwriting its access restrictions. The card flares bright, then settles to a steady glow. It no longer identifies as a specific access level — it identifies as ALL access levels.

The mineral dissolves into the stasis fluid, and the mixture crystallizes into a dense gel that absorbs energy on contact. A palm-sized blob that drinks power. Near Convergence systems, it creates a local dead zone.

You channel the disruptor's pulse through the siphon crystal. The crystal amplifies it a hundredfold — the device now emits a burst capable of overloading any energy system it's aimed at. One shot. Make it count.

The fungal extract reacts with the sedative compound, producing a paste that suppresses neural signatures. Smeared on your skin, it makes you invisible to anything that detects by energy pattern — including Echoes.

You align the two cipher fragments. The data patterns interlock — half the translation key is now complete. You can read simple alien text, but complex inscriptions still elude you. Two more fragments to go.
The refugee journal's margin notations complete a third of the cipher. The translation is becoming clearer — you can now read most operational text. One fragment remains.

The final fragment locks into place. The complete cipher unfolds in your mind like a language you always knew but forgot. Every alien inscription, every label, every record — readable. The universe just opened up.

You press the Choir crystal against the weapon core. The resonance frequency syncs — the core begins to hum, vibrating at the Convergence's own frequency. It's alive now, tuned to destroy the thing it was made to fight. Partially assembled. It needs a dampener and a power source.

The adapter accepts the navigation chip's crystalline format and bridges it to a universal power bus. The result is a device that can interface with any alien technology — Choir, Convergence, or the former civilization's systems. A skeleton key for machines.

You wire the overcharge device into the defense grid controller. The orbital satellites now have a targeting solution — and enough power for one devastating strike. Point it at the nexus and fire. Point it at the Choir ship and fire. Either way, everything changes.

You wrap the bio-fiber around the flare's head, creating a longer-burning light source. The alien fiber catches fire slowly and burns steady instead of blinding. A proper torch that'll last much longer than the flare alone.

You line the helmet's interior with the energy dampener gel. The dampener absorbs the worst of the Convergence's ambient radiation. Wearing this, you can survive the nexus's high-energy chambers without your nervous system frying.

You mount the tuning fork in the stabilizer's emitter array. The combined device doesn't just calm Echoes — it speaks their language. The stabilization field now carries your words as resonance patterns the dead can hear. And their responses come back clear.

The Choir power cell slots into the alien weapon's depleted energy chamber. The sidearm hums to life — fully charged now. Twenty shots instead of six. The four-armed grip is awkward, but the firepower is undeniable.

The energy dampener wraps around the primed core, containing its resonance while focusing its destructive potential. One more component — the siphon crystal fragment — and the countermeasure is complete.

The siphon crystal fragment snaps into the dampener housing like it was always meant to be there. The complete countermeasure weapon activates — a sphere of crystallized destruction, humming with the Convergence's own stolen energy turned against it. This kills planets. This saves them too.

objects.name: Your Broken Stasis Pod
objects.description: The pod that held you. Cracked open, amber fluid pooling beneath it.

then.text: Your stasis pod. The glass is spider-webbed with cracks, amber preservation fluid dripping from the breach. Inside, the padding still holds your shape. A thin layer of fluid coats the bottom — faintly luminescent, warm to the touch. Your specimen tag is clipped to the headrest.
The pod is empty now. Just cracked glass and drying fluid.
You push against the cracked glass. A shard breaks free — curved, sharp, the size of your palm. The fluid inside sloshes. You could collect some in the shard's hollow curve.
You scoop the warm amber fluid into the curved shard. It holds — barely. You seal it with a strip of pod padding. The fluid hums faintly against your skin.

You unclip the specimen tag from the headrest. It's labeled in alien script with what must be your catalogue number. A small holographic chip is embedded in the metal — your biometric data, recorded when they captured you.

objects.name: Stasis Pod Wall
objects.description: Hundreds of translucent pods stacked floor to ceiling, most containing dead specimens.

then.text: Hundreds of pods, stacked like cells in a honeycomb. Most hold dead things: creatures from dozens of worlds, suspended in amber fluid. A six-legged mammal. Something with translucent wings. A creature that might be a plant. All perfectly preserved, catalogued, filed away. A library of extinction. One cluster nearby has a control panel between the pods — it might tell you more.

objects.name: Metal Catwalks
objects.description: Narrow metal walkways connecting pod clusters across the vast hold.

then.text: Narrow walkways spanning the vertical hold. They connect pod clusters at different levels. The metal is an alloy you don't recognize — warm to the touch, faintly humming. The railing is built for beings much taller than you — your head barely clears the bottom rail. A catwalk leads toward a sealed door marked with what might be a biohazard symbol.
You follow the catwalk toward the sealed door. The containment corridor lies beyond.

objects.name: Floor Drain
objects.description: A drainage grate in the organic-metallic floor. Stasis fluid trickles into it.

then.text: A circular grate set into the floor. Amber fluid from your broken pod trickles down into darkness. The grate is sized for maintenance — large enough for a Choir drone to access the plumbing below, which means large enough for you. But the grate is bolted down.
The bolts are recessed and smooth — designed to be turned with a specific alien tool, not fingers. You can't get a grip.
The surgical probe's tip fits the recessed bolt heads. You work each one loose. The grate lifts away, revealing a maintenance shaft leading down. Cold air rises from below.

objects.name: Bioluminescent Wall Veins
objects.description: Green-glowing organic conduits running through the walls like blood vessels.

then.text: The walls are alive — or at least organic. Veins of bioluminescent material pulse with sickly green light, the ship's equivalent of emergency lighting. The glow pulses in a slow rhythm, like breathing. Where the veins branch, they form node-like clusters. The ship is as much organism as machine.
Warm. Faintly moist. The surface gives slightly under your touch, like pressing on skin. You pull your hand back. The glow brightens briefly where you touched it, then fades.

objects.name: Adjacent Stasis Pod
objects.description: A sealed pod next to yours, containing a large insect-like creature.

then.text: A specimen pod, sealed and functioning. Inside: a creature like a mantis crossed with a lobster, suspended in amber fluid. Its eyes are open. Dead? Or waiting? The pod's label has a number sequence — the Choir's cataloguing system. The number on this pod: 7-7-4-2.
The glass is much thicker than your pod's was — no cracks here. This one is working as intended. The creature inside doesn't react. Perfectly preserved. Perfectly imprisoned.

objects.name: Pod Cluster Controls
objects.description: Bio-organic control panel between the pod cluster. Fleshy buttons and tendon-like cables.

then.text: The control panel is disturbing. Buttons that look like blisters. Cables that look like tendons. A small display showing specimen data in alien script — vital signs, species classifications, preservation status. One readout is flashing amber: your pod. It knows you're gone.

You press buttons experimentally. The display cycles through specimen logs. Numbers repeat in a pattern — pod cluster identifiers, each a four-digit sequence. Your cluster: 7-7-4-2. The processing lab door across the hold has a similar keypad.
The display still cycles specimen data. Your pod's readout flashes amber — 'SPECIMEN ABSENT'. Nothing else useful here.

objects.name: Insect Specimen Pod
objects.description: A pod containing a large preserved insect-like creature.

then.text: A massive arthropod, easily twice your size. Compound eyes. Mandibles like bolt cutters. Six legs folded beneath a carapace of iridescent chitin. The specimen label shows a planet designation and a date — this creature was collected long before you.

objects.name: Empty Pod
objects.description: An empty stasis pod, cleaned and ready for a new specimen.

then.text: An empty pod, immaculately clean. Fresh amber fluid fills the reservoir below, waiting for the next specimen. The interior padding shows no wear. This pod was prepared recently. For someone. For you? Or for whatever comes next.
You climb inside the empty pod. It's cold. The padding molds to your body with unsettling precision. From inside, you could pass for a dormant specimen — at least to a quick visual scan.

objects.name: Processing Tubes
objects.description: Tubes connecting pods to a central processing unit, circulating preservation fluid.

then.text: Transparent tubes carrying amber fluid between pods and a central processor. The fluid flows in rhythmic pulses — the ship's heartbeat. Some tubes branch off toward the processing lab. The central node where they converge hums with a low, organic vibration.

objects.name: Alien Script Labels
objects.description: Labels on each pod written in the Choir's language.

then.text: Alien characters — angular, geometric, nothing like any human writing system. Numbers are recognizable by their pattern: 7-7-4-2 repeats on this cluster. The rest is meaningless to you. You'd need some kind of translation reference.

With the cipher, the labels resolve: species designation, homeworld coordinates, collection date, preservation status. Your pod reads: 'UNKNOWN BIPED — PLANET 7742 — RECENT ACQUISITION — STATUS: ESCAPED'. They know.

objects.name: Specimen Tag Reader
objects.description: A slot on the pod cluster where specimen tags are scanned.

then.text: A small slot with a faint amber glow — the same size as the specimen tags clipped to each pod. Some kind of scanner or reader. It might accept your tag.

You slot your tag into the reader. The display flickers — your biometric data scrolls past in alien script. A chime sounds. The system registers you as 'SPECIMEN IN TRANSIT'. For a moment, you are part of the Choir's inventory again. The nearby pod controls unlock additional data.

objects.name: Examination Table
objects.description: A surgical table with organic restraints. Stained with fluids you'd rather not identify.

then.text: A surgical table designed for specimens of various sizes — the restraints are adjustable, organic clamps that look grown rather than manufactured. Drainage channels run to the floor. The surface is stained with a dozen different colors of biological fluid. This is where the Choir takes specimens apart. The restraints are open. You could crawl under the table to hide.
You slide under the examination table. The space beneath is cramped but dark — the table's wide surface conceals you completely. You can see the room through the drainage slots.

objects.name: Surgical Tool Rack
objects.description: Curved bone-like instruments hanging from a wall mount. Alien surgical tools.

then.text: Surgical instruments, but nothing like human medicine. These tools look grown — curved like ribs, sharp like claws, organic and unsettling. A probe with a fine articulated tip catches your eye. It's the right size for your hands, unlike most things on this ship.

You take the surgical probe. It's lighter than it looks — warm, almost alive in your grip. The articulated tip responds to finger pressure, extending and retracting. A precision tool for a creature your size in a world built for giants.
The remaining tools are too large for you, or too specialized. The probe was the only useful one.

objects.name: Sample Jars
objects.description: Shelves of specimen samples in sealed containers.

then.text: Rows of sealed containers holding tissue samples, fluid samples, and small organ specimens from dozens of species. Labels in alien script. Some samples glow faintly. Others are disturbingly familiar in shape. One jar near the bottom — reachable for you — holds a small crystal that pulses with inner light.

objects.name: Lab Floor Drain
objects.description: Drainage system in the lab floor for cleaning biological waste.

then.text: A drainage grate, designed to wash away biological waste. The channels lead somewhere below — probably the waste processing level. Too small to fit through, even for you.

objects.name: Biological Data Screens
objects.description: Screens displaying alien biological data and specimen analysis.

then.text: Organic screens displaying scrolling alien data — biological diagrams, chemical formulas (maybe), and what looks like a scheduling system. The diagrams show dissection procedures for various species. One screen shows a startup routine: a sequence of bio-organic buttons lighting up in order. The lab door keypad uses the same buttons.

The screens detail specimen processing protocols. Species cataloguing. Preservation chemistry. And at the bottom: 'Next scheduled processing: SPECIMEN 7742-RECENT.' That's you. They're coming for you.

objects.name: Processing Lab Door
objects.description: A sealed door leading from the stasis hold to the processing lab.

then.text: A sealed door with a keypad of bio-organic buttons — the same type as the pod control panel. Four buttons, four digits. The biohazard symbol above the door suggests what's on the other side.
You press the buttons in the sequence from the pod controls: 7-7-4-2. The door hisses and slides open, revealing the processing lab beyond.
You press buttons randomly. A low buzzer sounds. Wrong code. You need to find the right sequence.

objects.name: Organic Corridor Walls
objects.description: The walls are ribbed like the inside of a throat, organic and mechanical in equal measure.

then.text: The corridor walls pulse faintly, ribs of organic material alternating with metallic panels. Like walking through the throat of something enormous. Condensation beads on every surface. The ribs contract slightly as you pass — the ship breathing around you.

objects.name: Floor Grating
objects.description: Metal floor grates revealing pulsing machinery beneath.

then.text: Through the grating, you can see machinery pulsing below — organic pumps, fluid conduits, things that look like muscles contracting and relaxing. The maintenance level. Unreachable from here, but the machinery hum is constant. It would cover small sounds.

objects.name: North Blast Door
objects.description: A sealed blast door leading deeper into the ship.

then.text: A massive blast door, sealed with bio-mechanical locks. Beyond this: the rest of the containment deck. The morgue, the feeding station, and deeper sections of the ship. A keycard slot glows faintly beside the door.
You hold the keycard to the slot. A pulse of amber light — and the blast door groans open, revealing the containment corridor beyond.
The door doesn't budge. Bio-mechanical locks hold it shut. You need some kind of access credential — a keycard, maybe, from the security hub.

objects.name: South Blast Door
objects.description: A blast door leading to the ventilation access and other sections.

then.text: This blast door is partially open — stuck in a halfway position. Something damaged its mechanism. You can squeeze through the gap, given your size. Beyond: more corridors, leading to the security hub and specimen archive.
You squeeze through the gap. The corridor branches — one path leads to the security hub, another to the specimen archive.

objects.name: Emergency Lighting
objects.description: Amber light strips running along the corridor ceiling.

then.text: Amber emergency lighting — not the main illumination. The ship is running on reduced power in this section. The light is enough to see by, but shadows pool in every recess and behind every rib. Good for hiding. Bad for spotting threats.

objects.name: Condensation Puddle
objects.description: A pool of condensation on the corridor floor.

then.text: Water — or something like water — condensed from the humid air. Your reflection looks up at you from the surface: small, battered, alone. In the reflection, you can see the ceiling above — and the outline of a ventilation grate you can't see from ground level.

objects.name: Specimen Storage Drawers
objects.description: Walls of drawers containing failed or expired specimens.

then.text: Rows of specimen drawers, like a morgue — because that's exactly what it is. Most are closed. A few are partially open, showing desiccated remains. The drawers are large enough for you to climb inside. Cold, dark, and deeply unpleasant, but an effective hiding spot.

You pull open an empty drawer and climb inside. It's freezing. The darkness is absolute when you pull it mostly closed. You can see a sliver of the room through the gap. The smell is chemical and wrong.

objects.name: Central Autopsy Slab
objects.description: A large slab for specimen examination, with drainage channels and tool mounts.

then.text: The central autopsy slab. Channels for fluid drainage. Mounting points for restraints and tools. The surface is clean — recently used and recently cleaned. Under the slab: a space large enough for you to curl up in, hidden by the slab's overhang.

objects.name: Recycling Vats
objects.description: Large vats where failed specimens are broken down into raw biological material.

then.text: Industrial-scale biological recycling. The vats bubble with enzymatic fluid that breaks down organic matter. The smell is acrid and sweet. The ship wastes nothing — failed specimens become raw material for the bio-garden, the hull repairs, the preservation fluid. Even in death, you'd be useful to them.

objects.name: Partially Open Drawer
objects.description: A specimen drawer left partially open. Something human-shaped is inside.

then.text: The drawer is open just enough to see inside. The shape is... human-sized. Not human, but close — bipedal, similar proportions. Withered. Dead for a long time. Whoever this was, they came from a world not unlike yours. Their clothes have pockets. Something glints inside one.

You pull the drawer fully open. The specimen is desiccated, mummified by the preservation process. In its pocket: a small data crystal, the same type used in the specimen archive. A personal log, maybe — from another prisoner who didn't make it.
You take the data crystal. It's warm — still holding charge after all this time. Whatever this person recorded, it survived them.

objects.name: Chemical Storage
objects.description: Shelves of preservation chemicals and biological agents.

then.text: Preservation chemicals in sealed containers. Most are labeled in alien script — dangerous without knowing what they are. One container is different: clear, gel-like, with a biohazard warning. It might be useful, but without understanding the labels, taking random chemicals seems unwise.

objects.name: Morgue Drainage System
objects.description: Floor drains connecting to the ship's waste processing system.

then.text: The drainage channels converge on a central grate. Below: the ship's waste processing level. You can hear the grinders from here — a low, rhythmic churning. Not a path you want to take.

objects.name: Nutrient Troughs
objects.description: Feeding troughs filled with grey nutrient paste for living specimens.

then.text: Troughs of grey nutrient paste. The Choir's universal feed — formulated to sustain any carbon-based organism. It smells like wet cardboard and tastes worse. But it's food, and you haven't eaten since they took you.
You scoop a tube's worth of the grey paste. Disgusting, but potentially useful — as food, as bait, or as a distraction. The Choir drones are programmed to respond to feeding station alerts.

objects.name: Automated Dispensers
objects.description: Machines that distribute nutrient paste on a schedule.

then.text: Automated nutrient dispensers connected to the central tank by flexible tubes. They operate on a timer — every few hours, paste flows into the troughs. The mechanism is simple: gravity feed from the tank, valve controlled by a timer circuit. The timer could be disrupted to trigger an early feed cycle — which would draw a maintenance drone to investigate.
You yank a feed tube loose. Nutrient paste sprays across the floor. An alarm chimes — a feeding station malfunction alert. A maintenance drone will come to fix this.

objects.name: Living Specimen Enclosures
objects.description: Energy-barrier pens holding living alien creatures.

then.text: Small enclosures behind shimmering energy barriers. Living creatures pace inside: a feline thing with too many eyes, a blob of translucent jelly that pulses with bioluminescence, something that looks like a walking plant. All captives, like you. None seem intelligent enough to help — but their pacing creates a background noise that masks small sounds.

You whisper to the creatures. The feline thing stops and stares at you with all seven eyes. The jelly blob pulses faster. The plant-thing ignores you entirely. None respond with anything resembling communication. But the feline's stare is unnervingly focused.

objects.name: Specimen Vitals Monitors
objects.description: Screens tracking the vital signs of living specimens.

then.text: Vital sign readouts for each specimen in the enclosures. Heart rates, respiration, neural activity — all in alien units, but the waveforms are recognizable. One screen shows YOUR vitals — they're still tracking you. Your heart rate spikes when you realize this.

objects.name: Central Nutrient Tank
objects.description: A massive tank storing the nutrient paste that feeds all specimens.

then.text: A large cylindrical tank of nutrient paste, connected to the dispensers by a network of tubes. There's a maintenance hatch at the base — small enough for you to squeeze through. Inside: a dark, paste-filled space where no one would think to look.
You open the maintenance hatch and crawl inside the space beneath the tank. It's cramped and smells terrible, but you're completely hidden. You can hear the paste gurgling above you.

objects.name: Feeding Schedule Console
objects.description: A control console managing the feeding schedule and specimen nutrition.

then.text: The feeding schedule console. Timers for each enclosure. Nutritional formulas adjusted per species. Your entry shows: 'ESCAPED — RECAPTURE PRIORITY: MEDIUM.' Medium. You're not even their top concern. That's somehow worse.

objects.name: Ventilation Shaft Walls
objects.description: Smooth organic walls with periodic ridges inside the ventilation system.

then.text: The ventilation shaft's walls are smooth organic material — the same living tissue as the ship's corridors, but narrower. Periodic ridges provide handholds. Red maintenance lighting gives everything a hellish glow. The shaft is sized for maintenance drones, which means it's comfortable for you. A rare advantage on this ship.

objects.name: Left Shaft Branch
objects.description: The ventilation shaft branches left, toward the security hub.

then.text: The left branch curves downward toward what the scratched map indicates is the security hub level. Air flows steadily from this direction — the security hub's ventilation is active.
You crawl through the left branch. The shaft narrows, then opens above a grate. Below: the security hub, screens glowing in the darkness.

objects.name: Right Shaft Branch
objects.description: The ventilation shaft branches right, toward the airlock bay.

then.text: The right branch slopes upward. Cold air flows from this direction — close to the hull. The scratched map suggests this leads toward the airlock bay level.
You crawl upward through the right branch. The air grows colder. The shaft ends at a grate overlooking the airlock bay.

objects.name: Scratch Marks
objects.description: Crude marks scratched into the shaft walls by previous escapees.

then.text: Someone scratched a crude map into the shaft wall. Arrows pointing in different directions with symbols: what might be an eye (security?), a circle with lines (airlock?), and a skull (danger). Someone was here before you. They mapped their escape route. Whether they made it out is another question.
You trace the scratched map onto your palm with a fingernail, memorizing the routes. Left toward security. Right toward the airlock. Straight down toward... the skull. You'll remember.

objects.name: Red Maintenance Light
objects.description: Dim red lighting strips running along the shaft.

then.text: Dim red strips — maintenance lighting for drone navigation. The red makes everything look like the inside of a wound. But it means the shaft is still actively maintained. Drones could come through here.

objects.name: Shaft Grate
objects.description: A removable grate at the shaft entrance.

then.text: The grate you entered through. You could close it behind you — hide the evidence of your passage. Or leave it open for a quick retreat.
You pull the grate shut behind you. From outside, it looks undisturbed. No one would know you came this way.

objects.name: Security Monitors
objects.description: Multiple screens showing surveillance feeds from the containment deck.

then.text: Surveillance feeds from throughout the containment deck. You can see the stasis hold (your broken pod visible), the processing lab, corridors, the feeding station. One screen shows The Curator on its rounds — tall, amber-eyed, methodical. It's currently three sections away. You can track its movements from here. Another screen shows a schematic: the ship's layout, deck by deck.

objects.name: Security Console
objects.description: Bio-organic control console for the security systems.

then.text: The main security console. Bio-organic buttons in a sequence panel — the same type as the lab door. The startup routine display on the lab screens showed buttons lighting up in order. If you saw that sequence, you could hack this console to override the containment locks.

You press the buttons in the sequence you memorized from the lab display. The console unlocks with a resonant chime. Containment locks across the deck disengage. You have access — and a keycard ejects from a slot.
The buttons respond to touch but you don't know the sequence. Random pressing triggers a security warning — amber lights flash. You back away quickly.

objects.name: Overturned Chair
objects.description: An alien chair knocked on its side. Evidence of a struggle.

then.text: An alien chair, knocked sideways. Designed for a much larger being — four leg-rests, a tall back with neural interface ports. Something happened here: a struggle, an escape attempt, a malfunction. Scorch marks on the floor nearby. Someone fought back. They lost.

objects.name: Cracked Monitor
objects.description: One security monitor with a cracked screen, still partially functional.

then.text: The cracked screen flickers between feeds. Through the static, you catch glimpses of a different deck — operational, not containment. A bridge. An engine room. A shuttle bay. The upper decks. If you could get past containment, there might be a way off this ship.

objects.name: Equipment Locker
objects.description: A storage locker for security equipment, partially open.

then.text: A security equipment locker, left ajar after whatever happened here. Most contents are alien and incomprehensible — restraint devices, scanning tools, things with no human equivalent. The locker is large enough to hide inside, and dark.
You climb inside the locker and pull the door mostly closed. Cold metal, pitch dark, but invisible to anything passing by.

objects.name: Inter-Deck Elevator
objects.description: An elevator connecting containment to the operational decks above.

then.text: The inter-deck elevator. It connects containment to the operational decks above — the bridge, engineering, shuttle bay. The door is sealed with a high-security bio-lock. The security console might be able to override it.
The security override worked — the elevator responds. The door opens with a hiss of pressurized air. Inside: a cylindrical chamber, controls for multiple decks. The operational levels await above.
The bio-lock doesn't respond to your touch. You need to hack the security console first.

objects.name: Data Crystal Archive
objects.description: Walls lined with thousands of glowing data crystals — the Choir's record of every species collected.

then.text: Thousands of data crystals in organic slots, floor to ceiling. Each one glows faintly — blue, green, amber. Each represents a species the Choir has catalogued. Some glow brighter than others. The dim ones... those worlds are already consumed. The scope is staggering. Hundreds of civilizations, reduced to crystal entries in a filing system.

objects.name: Crystal Reading Device
objects.description: A pedestal with a slot for reading data crystals.

then.text: A reading device on a pedestal. A crystal slot at the top, a holographic projector above. Insert a data crystal and its contents are displayed. The device is sized for Choir hands — the slot is high above you, but reachable if you stretch.

You slot the crystal into the reader. A holographic display blooms — alien text and images. It's a personal log from another specimen, recorded in a language you can partially decipher: dates, emotions, observations. They mapped parts of the ship. They found patterns in the Choir's language. Partial translations. A cipher fragment.

objects.name: Holographic Star Map
objects.description: Floating holographic displays showing catalogued worlds.

then.text: A holographic star map showing the Convergence's reach. Hundreds of star systems, most marked with a red symbol that can only mean one thing: consumed. A handful glow green — active harvesting sites. One of those green dots is the planet below you. The red ones stretch back across galaxies, across eons. The Convergence has been doing this since before most stars were born.

objects.name: Consumed Worlds Display
objects.description: A detailed display of worlds already drained by the Convergence.

then.text: Close-up data on consumed worlds. Before-and-after images: lush planets reduced to grey husks. The process takes years — the Convergence is patient. It drains slowly, completely, leaving nothing. Species data accompanies each world — a catalogue of extinction. One entry shows a species remarkably similar to the one on the planet below. Four-armed, tall, civilized. They built cities, wrote poetry, waged wars. All gone. Filed and forgotten.

objects.name: Personal Log Crystal Slot
objects.description: An empty slot where a data crystal was recently removed.

then.text: An empty slot in the crystal wall. The label reads — in alien script — something about a personal record. The crystal that was here was taken, or fell. It might be in the morgue, where the previous prisoner ended up.

objects.name: Archive Search Terminal
objects.description: A terminal for searching the specimen archive database.

then.text: A search terminal for the archive. Even without reading the language, the interface has visual search — you could search by shape, by world, by date. It might reveal information about the planet below, or about the Convergence itself.

You use the visual search, selecting the green-marked planet below. The archive returns results: the planet's species classification, its estimated remaining lifespan (rapidly decreasing), and a reference to something called 'The Nexus' — the Convergence's harvesting hub on the surface. The data includes coordinates.

objects.name: Airlock Blast Doors
objects.description: Heavy sealed blast doors to the secondary airlock.

then.text: Massive blast doors sealing the airlock. Through the viewport beside them: empty space, the planet below. The doors are magnetically sealed — the manual override panel might open them, but venting the bay to space would be catastrophic without a suit.

objects.name: Empty Docking Clamps
objects.description: Docking clamps where your ship, the Outrider, was once attached.

then.text: The docking clamps are open, empty. Your ship — the Outrider — was here. The Choir jettisoned it. Your way home, cast into the void. The clamps show scoring from forced separation. They didn't bother to undock properly. They just cut you loose.

objects.name: Emergency Suit Locker
objects.description: A locker containing alien emergency space suits.

then.text: An emergency suit locker — the universal symbol for vacuum protection is recognizable even in alien design. The suits inside are built for Choir physiology: too tall, too many limbs. But the helmet might be adaptable.
You open the locker. Three alien EVA suits hang inside — far too large for you. But the helmets are modular, designed to seal independently. One might fit over your head with some adjustment.

You detach the smallest helmet. It's still too big, but the internal padding adjusts automatically to your head shape. The seal isn't perfect, but it would give you minutes in vacuum or toxic atmosphere. Better than nothing.

objects.name: Manual Override Panel
objects.description: A heavily locked panel for manually controlling the airlock.

then.text: The airlock manual override. Heavy bio-mechanical locks — three of them. Emergency use only. From here you could open the blast doors, cycle the airlock, or trigger the docking sequence. But the locks need to be bypassed first.
The keycard disengages one of three locks. Two more remain. You'd need more tools — or a more powerful override — to open this fully.

objects.name: Viewport
objects.description: A large viewport showing the planet below — beautiful from orbit, dying from within.

then.text: The planet fills the viewport. Blue oceans, green continents, white cloud formations — it looks like paradise. But from orbit, you can see the Convergence's work: faint energy beams descending from relay platforms, connecting to the surface in a web of slow destruction. The atmosphere has a yellow tinge near the impact points. This world is beautiful. This world is dying. And somewhere down there, someone built a weapon to fight back.

objects.name: Airlock Control Console
objects.description: Controls for the airlock cycling and docking systems.

then.text: The airlock control console. Currently in standby — the manual override panel controls master access. The console shows docking status: 'BAY EMPTY — NO VESSEL DETECTED.' Your ship is gone. But the shuttle bay on the operational deck might have alternatives.

objects.name: Holographic Star Map
objects.description: A massive holographic projection showing the Convergence's path across galaxies.

then.text: The star map dominates the bridge — a holographic sphere showing hundreds of consumed systems marked in red, a handful of active harvesting sites in green, and the Convergence's projected path in white. The scale is galactic. The path stretches back billions of years. And it stretches forward, toward more systems, more civilizations, more worlds that don't know what's coming.

objects.name: Bridge Control Stations
objects.description: Organic mushroom-like consoles grown into the floor.

then.text: Control stations grown from the floor like mushrooms — organic interfaces with bio-luminescent displays. Each station manages a different ship system. Most are locked to Choir biometrics. But the navigation station has a data port where a chip could be extracted.
You crawl under a control station, hidden in the hollow base. The mushroom cap above provides perfect cover — the Choir designed these for standing operators, not for anyone crouching underneath.

objects.name: Command Throne
objects.description: The captain's seat with neural interface tendrils dangling from the headrest.

then.text: The command throne. A seat grown from the ship itself, with neural interface tendrils hanging from the headrest. The Choir commander connects directly to the ship through this chair — seeing through its sensors, feeling its hull, commanding its systems with thought. The tendrils twitch faintly, reaching for a mind that isn't there.

You climb onto the throne. The seat is absurdly large — you sit in it like a child in an adult's chair. The tendrils reach for your head but can't quite connect — wrong biology. They brush your skin and you feel a jolt: images flash. The ship's name. Its mission. The planet below, marked for consumption. Then the connection breaks. Too alien. But you glimpsed something useful.

objects.name: Bridge Viewport
objects.description: The main viewport showing the planet with energy siphons descending from orbit.

then.text: From the bridge viewport, the harvesting operation is visible in horrifying detail. Energy siphons descend from orbital platforms to the planet surface like luminous tentacles. Where they touch down, the atmosphere yellows and the land greys. The planet is being drained alive. And from here, you can see the nexus — a crystalline mountain at the convergence point of all the siphons. The heart of the operation.

objects.name: Navigation Console
objects.description: The ship's navigation system with a removable navigation chip.

then.text: The navigation console. Star charts, course plots, jump coordinates — all in alien notation, but the mathematics of navigation is universal. A small crystalline chip glows in a slot: the navigation data core. It contains the ship's entire star chart database. Removable.

You pull the navigation chip from its slot. The console goes dark — without this chip, the ship can't navigate. The chip is warm in your hand, pulsing with data. Star charts for hundreds of systems. Jump coordinates. And the route home.

objects.name: Star Chart Display
objects.description: Detailed star charts showing the Convergence's harvesting route.

then.text: Detailed star charts. The Convergence's route is mapped across galaxies — a path of consumption stretching back billions of years. Ahead on the path: more inhabited systems. Earth's sector isn't on the immediate route, but it's close enough to matter. The charts also show comm frequencies used by the Choir for inter-ship communication.

objects.name: Organic Reactor
objects.description: A massive pulsing organic reactor — the ship's power source, like a beating heart.

then.text: The reactor is alive. A massive organic structure wrapped in mechanical cables, pulsing like a heart. Each beat sends power through the ship. The sound is deep, rhythmic, almost comforting in its regularity. Coolant flows through transparent tubes, glowing blue-white. The reactor's rhythm masks other sounds — a natural sound-masking zone.

objects.name: Coolant System
objects.description: Transparent tubes carrying glowing coolant fluid throughout engineering.

then.text: Coolant tubes running from the reactor to the hull. The fluid glows a soft blue-white — cold to the touch. A small valve near the floor controls a secondary coolant line. A flask of this coolant could be useful — it's cold enough to freeze organic material on contact.
You open the valve and fill a small container from the emergency kit nearby. The coolant is intensely cold — your fingers go numb holding it. Cap it quickly. This stuff could freeze flesh on contact.

objects.name: Maintenance Drones
objects.description: Small spider-like robots crawling over engine surfaces, performing repairs.

then.text: Spider-like maintenance drones, each the size of a cat. They crawl over surfaces, welding, cleaning, repairing. They ignore you — you're not engineering equipment. But they'll report anomalies to the Curator. One is damaged, trailing a broken antenna. That antenna could be useful for detecting Choir signals.

You snatch the broken antenna from the damaged drone as it passes. It doesn't react — the damage is in its sensor array, and it can't detect the theft. The antenna is a thin crystalline rod, still faintly resonating with Choir frequencies.

objects.name: Steam Vents
objects.description: Periodic steam vents releasing excess heat from the reactor.

then.text: Steam vents releasing reactor heat in periodic bursts. The timing is regular — every thirty seconds. The steam cloud provides brief concealment and adds to the ambient noise. Time your movements to the vents and you're harder to detect.

objects.name: Power Junction
objects.description: A power distribution node where the reactor's output is routed to different ship systems.

then.text: A power distribution node. Energy from the reactor is split here and routed to different ship systems. One line leads to the shuttle bay. Another to containment. A removable power cell sits in a charging cradle — portable energy, designed for field equipment.

You lift the power cell from its cradle. It's heavy for its size, warm, humming with stored energy. An alarm chirps once — a maintenance alert, not a security alarm. But someone might notice a missing power cell on the next maintenance cycle.

objects.name: Engineering Console
objects.description: Master engineering console for monitoring reactor systems.

then.text: The engineering master console. Reactor status, power output, system diagnostics. Everything reads nominal — the ship is operating perfectly. A toggle panel on the right controls power routing to secondary systems. Shuttle bay power could be redirected... if you knew which toggles to flip.

objects.name: Communication Dish
objects.description: A dish-like apparatus suspended in the room's center, surrounded by crystalline amplifiers.

then.text: The main communication dish. It transmits and receives across interstellar distances using a technology you don't fully understand — crystalline amplification of subsonic resonance, somehow carried through subspace. The dish is pointed at a distant star system — the Convergence's next target. The amplifiers around it hum with latent energy.

objects.name: Crystalline Amplifiers
objects.description: Glowing crystals that amplify communications signals.

then.text: Crystalline amplifiers — they boost the comm signal to interstellar range. The technology is elegant: each crystal resonates at a specific frequency, and together they form a harmonic that can carry data across light-years. The schematics for this system would be invaluable.

objects.name: Communication Consoles
objects.description: Wall consoles for targeting and managing transmissions.

then.text: Communication targeting consoles. From here, the Choir aims transmissions at specific star systems. The interface shows recent transmission logs — reports to the Convergence about harvesting progress. The console also has a technical schematics drawer.

You pull open the schematics drawer. Inside: crystalline data sheets showing the comm array's design — frequencies, power requirements, targeting algorithms. This could be used to build or hijack a transmission system.

objects.name: Recording Station
objects.description: Where the Choir logs reports to the Convergence.

then.text: A recording station with an alien microphone-like device. The Choir logs their harvesting reports here — progress updates sent to the greater Convergence entity. Recent logs are stored locally before transmission.

You play back recent recordings. The Choir's subsonic voices are felt more than heard — deep vibrations that make your bones ache. You can't understand the words, but the tone is clear: efficiency, routine, cold purpose. One recording mentions specimen containment anomalies. They know something escaped.

objects.name: Black Box Terminal
objects.description: A terminal where the ship's flight recorder data is stored.

then.text: The ship's flight recorder terminal. The black box contains the complete history of this vessel — every system visited, every specimen collected, every communication. A portable copy is stored in a removable crystal module. Proof of everything the Choir has done.

You eject the portable black box crystal. It's dense, heavy for its size, and warm with stored data. This is evidence — proof of the Convergence's existence, the Choir's operations, and the harvesting of countless worlds. It could also prove your own sentience to the Curator, if it came to that.

objects.name: Signal Transmission Log
objects.description: A log of all signals sent and received by the comm array.

then.text: A transmission log. Thousands of entries stretching back millennia. The most recent entries show communications with the nexus on the planet below. Signal frequencies, timestamps, protocols. This information could help override the comm system later.

objects.name: Weapon Racks
objects.description: Racks of alien weapons — resonance staffs, energy projectors, containment nets.

then.text: Racks of Choir weapons. Resonance staffs — long poles that emit disorienting subsonic pulses. Energy projectors — compact devices that fire concentrated light. Containment nets — woven from energy-reactive fibers. All biometrically locked to Choir physiology. Your hands can't activate any of them. But not everything here is a weapon...
You press your hand to a weapon lock. Nothing. The biometric scanner flashes red — wrong species, wrong everything. These weapons are useless to you.

objects.name: Resonance Equipment Rack
objects.description: A separate rack holding resonance-based tools, not all of which are weapons.

then.text: A rack of resonance equipment. Not all weapons — some are tools. A resonance disruptor catches your eye: a handheld device designed to disrupt Choir bio-mechanical locks. It's a maintenance tool, not a weapon, which means it's not biometrically locked. The Choir don't restrict access to their own repair equipment.

You take the resonance disruptor. It vibrates in your hand — alive with subsonic energy. Point it at a Choir lock, press the trigger, and the lock's bio-mechanism scrambles. A skeleton key for an alien ship. This changes everything.

objects.name: Weapon Maintenance Bench
objects.description: A workbench for maintaining and repairing Choir weapons.

then.text: A maintenance workbench with alien tools for weapon repair. The bench is high — chest-height for you — but there's space underneath to hide. Tools are organized with military precision.
You slide under the workbench. Dark, cramped, but completely hidden from view. You can see the room through gaps in the bench's framework.

objects.name: Damaged Weapons Bin
objects.description: A bin containing broken and damaged Choir weapons awaiting recycling.

then.text: Broken weapons awaiting recycling. Cracked resonance staffs, depleted energy cells, a containment net with melted fibers. Useless as weapons. But broken equipment often contains useful components — energy cells, focusing crystals, conductive materials.

objects.name: Empty Rack Slot
objects.description: One weapon rack has an empty slot — something was removed recently.

then.text: One slot in the weapon rack is empty. The outline suggests a heavy weapon — an energy projector, maybe. Recently removed. Someone or something is armed and active elsewhere on the ship. The Curator's extra firepower, perhaps.

objects.name: Armory Biometric Lock
objects.description: A biometric security lock on the main weapon racks.

then.text: A biometric lock requiring Choir biology to open. It scans for the Choir's unique neural signature. No amount of hacking will trick it — you'd need actual Choir tissue.

You press the severed tendril against the scanner. It pulses — residual neural activity. The lock hesitates, then clicks open. The main weapon racks unlock. Most weapons are still useless to you — wrong biology for the triggers. But with full access, you can search more thoroughly.

objects.name: Dormant Alcoves
objects.description: Wall recesses where the Choir stand dormant, connected to the ship via neural tendrils.

then.text: Alcoves in the walls where the Choir rest — if you can call it rest. They stand upright, connected to the ship by tendrils from their backs. Eyes closed (they have no eyes — the blank faces are somehow worse). They're dormant but not dead. You can see their bodies pulse with the ship's rhythm. One alcove is empty. One tendril hangs loose, severed — a malfunction or a conflict.

objects.name: Resonance Chamber
objects.description: A central circular depression where the Choir communicate through subsonic vibration.

then.text: The communal resonance chamber — a depression in the floor that glows with subsonic energy. This is how the Choir speak: through vibration, felt in the bones rather than heard. The patterns in the vibration are complex, layered. Something is recorded in the chamber's surface — etched by resonance over time. It might be readable with the right tool.

You step into the resonance chamber. The vibrations pass through you — not painful, but deeply disorienting. For a moment, you feel the echoes of Choir communication: patterns, frequencies, something that might be language. And in the resonance residue, a pattern repeats — a cipher fragment, worn into the chamber's surface by centuries of use.

You trace the resonance pattern onto your palm, memorizing the second cipher fragment. Combined with the first from the personal log, you're beginning to understand the Choir's writing system. Two of four pieces.

objects.name: Geometric Wall Patterns
objects.description: Intricate geometric patterns covering the walls — art, language, or both.

then.text: The walls are covered in geometric patterns — spirals, fractals, interlocking shapes. Are they art? Language? Navigation charts? Maps of consciousness? Without context, they're beautiful and incomprehensible. The Choir's inner world, displayed for no one who could understand it.

objects.name: Severed Neural Tendril
objects.description: A neural tendril hanging loose from an empty alcove, still faintly active.

then.text: A neural tendril hanging from an empty alcove, severed at one end. It's still faintly active — twitching, reaching for a connection that isn't there. The cut is clean. Someone or something severed it deliberately. The tissue still carries residual Choir neural signatures.

You pull the tendril free. It writhes in your grip — still alive, still seeking connection. Deeply unpleasant to hold, but Choir biometric locks scan for neural signatures. This dead tissue might still register.

objects.name: Choir Personal Artifact
objects.description: A small object on a shelf — the Choir equivalent of a personal possession.

then.text: A small crystalline object on a recessed shelf — the only individual possession visible in the quarters. It's shaped like a spiral, smooth, warm. A memento? A tool? A religious object? The Choir are more than machines. They have... something. Whether it's sentiment or programming, you can't tell.

objects.name: Passage to Other Decks
objects.description: A corridor leading from the quarters to other operational sections.

then.text: A passage leading to the operational sections of the ship. From here, you can reach the shuttle bay, hydroponics, the data core, and waste processing. The passage is well-lit and wide — a main Choir thoroughfare. You'll need to be careful.

objects.name: Damaged Shuttle
objects.description: A beetle-shaped Choir shuttle with visible damage — panels removed, missing a power cell.

then.text: The damaged shuttle. Panels are removed, exposing its innards. The cockpit is intact but the power cell cradle is empty and a fuel line is disconnected. With a power cell and fuel line reconnected, this thing might fly. It's your best chance at reaching the planet surface.

You slot the power cell into the cradle. The shuttle's systems flicker to life — instrument panels glow, the cockpit hums. But the fuel line is still disconnected. Two more steps: fuel line and navigation initialization.
You reconnect the fuel line. Liquid fuel flows from the bay's supply into the shuttle's tanks. The engine indicator turns green. One more step: the navigation system needs initialization.

You slot the navigation chip into the shuttle's nav console. Star charts load. The shuttle's AI calculates a descent trajectory to the planet surface. The shuttle is ready. When you launch, there's no coming back to this ship.

You climb into the cockpit and seal the hatch. The shuttle's engines engage. The bay door opens to space. You hit the launch trigger. The shuttle rockets forward, out of the bay, banking hard toward the planet below. Behind you, amber lights flash — the Curator knows. But you're already falling toward the atmosphere. The ship shrinks behind you. The planet fills your view. Phase transition: Descent.

objects.name: Intact Shuttle Alpha
objects.description: A functional Choir shuttle in its docking cradle.

then.text: An intact Choir shuttle — beetle-shaped, sleek. The cockpit is sealed with biometric locks. You can't get in without Choir biology or a resonance disruptor.

objects.name: Intact Shuttle Beta
objects.description: A second functional Choir shuttle.

then.text: Another intact shuttle. Sealed tight. The damaged one is your best option — its locks are already broken.

objects.name: Launch Mechanism
objects.description: Docking mechanisms and launch rails for the shuttles.

then.text: Launch rails and docking mechanisms. The system is automated — once a shuttle is powered and the bay door opens, the launch sequence handles the rest. The bay door controls are in the control booth above.

objects.name: Bay Door
objects.description: A massive door opening to space.

then.text: The shuttle bay door. Beyond it: vacuum, stars, and the planet below. The door is controlled from the booth. Opening it without a sealed shuttle cockpit would be instantly fatal.

objects.name: Control Booth
objects.description: An elevated control booth overlooking the shuttle bay.

then.text: An elevated control booth with windows overlooking the bay. From there, you can manage bay door operations and shuttle launches. The booth also provides a hidden vantage point — small, enclosed, with visibility over the entire bay.

objects.name: Shuttle Fueling Lines
objects.description: Fuel supply lines connecting to shuttle docking cradles.

then.text: Fuel supply lines for the shuttle docking cradles. One line near the damaged shuttle is disconnected — it was removed during repairs and never reconnected. The loose end could be taken.
You detach the disconnected fuel line. It's flexible, about four feet long, with self-sealing connectors at both ends. Designed to snap into the shuttle's fuel intake.

objects.name: Alien Plant Rows
objects.description: Rows of strange alien plants in nutrient baths.

then.text: Rows of alien plants in glowing nutrient baths. Some bioluminesce in blue and green. Some have tendrils that sway without wind. Some look carnivorous. The plants are dense enough to hide among — their canopy would conceal something your size. This is the closest thing to beauty on the ship, and it's still deeply wrong.
You push into the plant rows, crouching among the bioluminescent stalks. The leaves close around you, reacting to your body heat. You're invisible in the green glow.

objects.name: Nutrient Baths
objects.description: Glowing liquid baths feeding the alien plants.

then.text: The nutrient baths glow faintly green — the same base fluid used in stasis pods, but modified for plant growth. The plants drink eagerly, their roots reaching deep into the solution.

objects.name: Biological Growth Vats
objects.description: Large vats producing biological components used throughout the ship.

then.text: Growth vats producing raw biological material — hull patch compounds, neural tissue, organic circuitry. The ship literally grows its own replacement parts. The vats bubble and churn, producing material that's harvested on a schedule.

objects.name: Plant Harvest Station
objects.description: A station with cutting tools for harvesting bio-garden materials.

then.text: A harvest station with curved cutting tools. The bio-garden's products are processed here — fibers separated, extracts distilled, compounds prepared. Bundles of harvested plant fiber sit ready for processing. Strong, flexible stuff.
You take a bundle of bio-garden fiber. It's incredibly strong — you can't tear it by hand. Woven or braided, it could reinforce almost anything.

objects.name: Carnivorous Plant
objects.description: A large plant with maw-like flowers that snap at movement.

then.text: A large carnivorous plant with maw-like flowers. The flowers snap shut when they detect movement — fast enough to catch small creatures. Definitely don't reach inside. But the plant produces a concentrated extract from its prey — a potent biochemical compound.

You squeeze nutrient paste into a maw. The flower snaps shut, processing the paste eagerly. While it's occupied, you scrape concentrated extract from the plant's distillation organ — a thick, amber liquid with potent biochemical properties.

objects.name: Bioluminescent Blooms
objects.description: Flowers that glow brilliantly in shifting blue and purple patterns.

then.text: Bioluminescent flowers, shifting through blue and purple in slow waves. They're breathtaking — the only genuinely beautiful thing you've seen on this ship. The light patterns seem almost deliberate, like a language of color. You watch, mesmerized, before remembering where you are.

objects.name: Organic Brain Core
objects.description: The ship's central computer — a massive organic brain suspended in fluid.
