then.text: The ship's brain. Literally. A massive organic structure suspended in translucent fluid, connected to every system by thousands of neural cables. It pulses with thought — you can see electrochemical patterns rippling across its surface. This is the ship's consciousness: navigation, life support, communications, security. Everything flows through this brain. And somewhere in its folds, the Choir's deepest secrets are stored.

objects.name: Neural Cable Network
objects.description: Thousands of neural cables connecting the brain to the ship's systems.

then.text: Neural cables spreading from the brain to every wall, floor, and ceiling — the ship's nervous system. Each cable carries data, commands, sensory input. The cables are warm and faintly pulsing. They're organic, like everything else on this ship.

objects.name: Interface Terminals
objects.description: Terminals around the perimeter for accessing the data core.

then.text: Interface terminals for querying the data core. The Choir interact with their central brain through these terminals — requesting data, issuing commands, reviewing logs. The terminals require a resonance handshake to activate.

The resonance disruptor bypasses the handshake. The terminal activates, flooding you with data: Convergence communications, harvesting schedules, specimen logs. And deep in the data stream — a resonance crystal containing the Choir's command frequencies. You download it.

objects.name: Data Flow Conduits
objects.description: Transparent conduits carrying visible data through glowing fluid.

then.text: Data flows visibly through transparent conduits — pulses of bioluminescent light carrying information through liquid medium. You can see the data move: fast pulses for commands, slow waves for background processes. When the brain thinks hard, the conduits blaze with activity.

objects.name: Core Access Panel
objects.description: A maintenance panel providing direct access to the brain's housing.

then.text: A maintenance access panel on the brain's housing tank. Through the panel, you could reach the brain directly — dangerous, but it would allow a deeper interface than the terminals provide.

objects.name: Data Flow Monitor
objects.description: A display showing the brain's processing activity in real-time.

then.text: A real-time display of the brain's activity. Current processing: harvesting telemetry, specimen containment status (your escape is flagged), Convergence communications, and something marked 'PRIORITY OVERRIDE' that you can't read without the cipher.

objects.name: Crashed Shuttle
objects.description: Your stolen Choir shuttle, half-buried in grey soil after a rough landing.

then.text: The shuttle — or what's left of it. Half-buried in grey, nutrient-depleted soil. One wing sheared off during the crash. Smoke rises from the engine housing. The cockpit is intact, and you can see through the cracked windshield. Supplies might still be salvageable inside.

objects.name: Sheared Wing
objects.description: The shuttle's torn-off wing, embedded in the soil.

then.text: The shuttle's wing, torn free on impact and embedded in the dead soil twenty meters from the main wreck. The alloy is bent and scorched. Nothing salvageable here — just evidence of how close you came to not surviving the landing.

objects.name: Dead Soil
objects.description: The planet's surface — grey, cracked, drained of all nutrients.

then.text: Grey soil. No color, no life, no moisture. The Convergence has drained everything — nutrients, water, energy at the molecular level. The ground crunches under your feet like ash. This was once a living world. A few years from now, it will be a grey husk drifting in space.

objects.name: Distant City
objects.description: The silhouette of a ruined city on the horizon.

then.text: A city on the horizon. Towers and spires in an alien architectural style — elegant, sweeping curves. Dark against the yellow-green sky. It looks intact from here, but the silence tells you everything. No lights. No movement. No sound. A dead city on a dying world. But the archive data said the planet's defenders built their weapon there. That's where you need to go.

objects.name: Energy Siphon Beams
objects.description: Massive energy beams descending from orbital platforms to the planet surface.

then.text: Energy siphon beams from orbit — visible even from the ground. Pillars of light descending from the sky, connecting to siphon towers on the surface. They hum at a frequency you feel in your chest. The beams converge in the distance, toward the nexus. The planet's energy flows up through these beams, off-world, feeding the Convergence.

objects.name: Shuttle Debris Field
objects.description: Scattered debris from the shuttle crash landing.

then.text: Scattered debris from the crash — panels, insulation, broken instruments. Most is useless, but you spot a signal flare among the wreckage — standard emergency equipment, designed to be visible from orbit.

objects.name: Cockpit Instruments
objects.description: Flickering shuttle cockpit instruments, partially functional.

then.text: The cockpit instruments flicker between functionality and static. Navigation: offline. Communications: offline. Life support: minimal. Emergency beacon: standby. The shuttle can't fly, but some systems still work. The emergency beacon could recall the shuttle to a safe location — if there's a safe location to recall it to.

objects.name: Emergency Supply Compartment
objects.description: A compartment of emergency supplies, thrown open during the crash.

then.text: Emergency supplies scattered across the cockpit floor during the crash. Choir emergency rations (inedible for you), a repair kit (alien tools), and buried under the mess — a signal flare designed to be visible from orbit.

You dig out the signal flare. It's cylindrical, with a chemical ignition trigger. Pull the cap and it burns with intense white-hot light for about 30 seconds. Visible from orbit, audible from a kilometer away. A beacon or a distraction.

objects.name: Navigation System
objects.description: The shuttle's damaged navigation system, partially functional.

then.text: The navigation system is damaged but partially functional. It shows your crash location and a rough map of the surrounding terrain. The dead city is 12 kilometers northeast. The nearest siphon tower is 3 kilometers south. A refugee camp signature is 5 kilometers west.

objects.name: Cracked Windshield
objects.description: The shuttle's windshield, cracked but intact. The wasteland stretches beyond.

then.text: Through the cracked windshield: the grey wasteland stretches to the horizon. The sky is a sickly yellow-green. Siphon beams descend in the distance. And the ruined city waits on the horizon, dark and silent. You're on your own now. No ship, no allies, no plan. Just a dying planet and whatever you can carry.

objects.name: Personal Items
objects.description: Items from your ship, the Outrider, that somehow ended up in the shuttle.

then.text: Items from your ship — the Outrider. A photograph of someone you loved. A coffee mug, chipped. A salvage operator's multitool (broken). How did these get here? The Choir must have transferred them with you, cataloguing your possessions alongside your biology. Even your memories are specimens to them.

objects.name: Emergency Beacon Kit
objects.description: The shuttle's emergency beacon system, still functional.

then.text: The shuttle's emergency beacon system. Still functional on backup power. Activating it would broadcast a homing signal — the shuttle could be recalled to a safe location by anyone with the right frequency. A lifeline for later. Or a signal that draws attention.

You detach the portable emergency beacon. Small, self-powered, with a single-use recall transmitter. Activate it, and any shuttle tuned to this frequency will home to the signal. Your escape ticket — if you survive long enough to use it.

objects.name: Cracked Wasteland Ground
objects.description: Drained, lifeless soil cracked into geometric patterns.

then.text: The ground is cracked into geometric patterns — hexagonal, like a dried lakebed. Every drop of moisture, every nutrient, every trace of biological energy has been extracted. You're walking on a corpse.

objects.name: Petrified Alien Trees
objects.description: Dead alien vegetation frozen in place, drained of all life.

then.text: Petrified alien trees — frozen mid-growth, drained of every molecule of water and energy. Their bark is stone-hard, their leaves are brittle crystal. They shatter at a touch. A forest turned to sculpture by the Convergence's hunger.

objects.name: Crystalline Mineral Growths
objects.description: Strange crystal formations where the Convergence's energy mineralized the soil.

then.text: Crystalline growths jutting from the soil — where the Convergence's energy saturated the ground, the minerals transformed into crystal. They hum faintly with residual energy. The formations are sharp, beautiful, and deeply wrong — crystallized soil that was once farmland.

objects.name: Exposed Root Systems
objects.description: Desiccated root systems of dead alien vegetation, exposed by soil erosion.

then.text: Root systems exposed by erosion — the topsoil was eaten away when the Convergence drained it. The roots are dry as paper, crumbling at a touch. Whatever once grew here had deep, complex root networks — a sign of a rich ecosystem, now reduced to fossil.

objects.name: Alien Path Marker
objects.description: A weathered marker stone along what was once a maintained path.

then.text: A path marker — this was once a road. The marker has alien script and what might be distance indicators. The path leads toward the city. Someone maintained this route. Someone walked here every day. Now it leads through a graveyard.

objects.name: Approaching City
objects.description: The ruined city growing larger on the horizon.

then.text: The city is closer now. You can make out individual buildings — elegant spires, arched bridges, crystalline domes. The architecture is beautiful in a way that makes the emptiness worse. This was a civilization at its peak. Then the Convergence came.
You continue toward the city. The path is clear but the terrain is treacherous — cracked ground and crystal formations. The gates loom ahead.

objects.name: Siphon Tower
objects.description: A massive crystalline energy siphon tower, hundreds of meters tall.

then.text: The siphon tower up close is terrifying. Hundreds of meters of crystal, driving deep into the planet's crust. Energy crackles up its surface in visible arcs — the stolen life force of a world, being pumped into orbit. The hum is deafening. Your teeth ache. The air shimmers with power. A crystal fragment at the base has cracked free — raw Convergence energy in crystalline form.

objects.name: Scorched Earth
objects.description: The ground around the tower is scorched black and glassed smooth.

then.text: The ground within a hundred meters of the tower is glassed — fused by energy into a smooth, dark surface. Your reflection stares up from it. Nothing grows here. Nothing can. The energy is too intense. You tread carefully.

objects.name: Relay Nodes
objects.description: Smaller crystalline nodes relaying energy to the main tower.

then.text: Smaller crystal nodes surrounding the main tower, collecting and relaying energy from a wider area. They pulse in sync with the tower's rhythm. The network is efficient — no energy wasted, no area untapped. The planet is being drained systematically, node by node.

objects.name: Tower Base
objects.description: The base of the siphon tower where it meets the ground.

then.text: The tower's base, where crystal meets earth. The crystal has grown INTO the ground, merging with the bedrock. Near the junction, a fragment has cracked free from stress — a shard of pure siphon crystal, still crackling with stored planetary energy. It's dangerously powerful. And potentially very useful.

You pry the crystal fragment loose. It burns your fingers — not heat, but energy. The shard crackles with stolen planetary power, arcing tiny lightning bolts. You wrap it in cloth to handle it. This is raw Convergence energy. Component material for a weapon that could hurt them back.

objects.name: Energy Field
objects.description: A visible field of energy surrounding the tower, distorting the air.

then.text: The energy field distorts everything within it — light bends, shadows twist, your vision blurs. Getting too close would be dangerous without protection. The radiation badge from the bunker could help you gauge safe distances.

objects.name: Transformed Mineral Deposits
objects.description: Soil transformed into strange minerals by the Convergence's energy.

then.text: The soil near the tower has been transformed by energy saturation into a crystalline mineral — not the same as the tower's crystal, but related. It has dampening properties, absorbing and dissipating energy. Combined with the right catalyst, it could create a localised energy suppression field.

You chip off a sample of the transformed mineral. It's cool to the touch — actively absorbing ambient energy. The opposite of the siphon crystal. Where the crystal stores energy, this mineral dampens it. Together, they might be used to control or neutralize Convergence power.

objects.name: Collapsed Shelters
objects.description: The remains of refugee shelters, built from alien materials.

then.text: Collapsed shelters — temporary structures built from lightweight alien material. The refugees fled here from the city. They set up a camp, built barricades, tried to survive. The shelters are big enough to hide inside — rubble provides cover.
You crawl into a collapsed shelter. The debris forms a natural cave — cramped, dark, but hidden from view. You're invisible here.

objects.name: Abandoned Possessions
objects.description: Personal items dropped during a panicked evacuation.

then.text: Scattered alien possessions. Clothing designed for four-armed beings. Tools. Children's items — small, colorful objects that might be toys. A cooking vessel, still holding desiccated food. These people left in a hurry. They took what they could carry and ran.

objects.name: Makeshift Barricade
objects.description: A crude defensive barrier facing toward the city.

then.text: A barricade of debris and scavenged material, facing the city. They were defending against something coming FROM the city — the Echoes, maybe, or Convergence constructs. The barricade is breached. Whatever they were defending against got through.

objects.name: Alien Skeletons
objects.description: Remains of the planet's former inhabitants — tall, thin, four-armed.

then.text: Skeletons. Tall, thin, four-armed. The planet's former inhabitants. They died here, at their barricade, defending their camp. Some are in positions suggesting they fell fighting. Others are curled up, as if they just stopped. The Convergence's energy drain doesn't just kill the land. It kills everything.

objects.name: Supply Cache
objects.description: A partially buried cache of survival supplies and equipment.

then.text: A supply cache, partially buried and sealed. The refugees stored survival equipment here — rations, tools, climbing gear. The seal is intact. The supplies inside should still be usable.
You break the seal and open the cache. Inside: preserved rations, climbing pitons, and various alien tools. The refugees planned for a long stay. They didn't get one.
You take the rations and climbing pitons. Alien food — different from the Choir's paste, actually palatable. The pitons are designed for four-armed climbers but work fine with two hands.

objects.name: Refugee Records
objects.description: A pile of journals and records left by the refugees.

then.text: Journals and records. The refugees documented everything — the Convergence's arrival, the evacuation, the city's fall, their attempts to survive. One journal stands out: detailed, scientific, written by someone who understood what was happening. It contains observations about the Convergence's patterns. And within its pages — the third cipher fragment.

You take the scientist's journal. Its pages are brittle but legible. The observations are meticulous — energy readings, pattern analyses, linguistic comparisons between the Choir's writing and the planet's own script. The third cipher fragment is here, recorded by someone who was trying to crack the same code.

objects.name: Giant Alien Fungi
objects.description: Massive bioluminescent mushrooms that survived the Convergence's drain.

then.text: Massive fungi, caps glowing purple and blue. They survive because they feed on decay — the Convergence's destruction is their nutrient source. Ironic. The largest have been hollowed out and used as shelters. Their bioluminescence provides light. Their spores fill the air with a gentle, medicinal scent. A grove of survivors, thriving on catastrophe.

You duck inside a hollowed mushroom cap. The interior is warm, dry, and lit by the fungus's own glow. Someone lived here — there are marks of occupation, a sleeping spot, a small fire pit. A safe place.

objects.name: Luminescent Spore Clouds
objects.description: Lazy clouds of glowing spores drifting through the grove.

then.text: Spore clouds drift lazily through the grove, glowing softly. They're not harmful — actually, they have mild antiseptic properties. The planet's former inhabitants probably used them medicinally. Breathing them in clears your head.

objects.name: Hollowed Mushroom Shelter
objects.description: A large fungus hollowed out and used as a shelter by a previous survivor.

then.text: A mushroom cap hollowed into a shelter. Inside: marks of habitation. Someone lived here for a while — sleep marks in the soft fungal floor, a small fire pit, crude shelves carved into the cap wall. And on those shelves: jars of fungal extract, carefully harvested.
You take a jar of fungal extract. Concentrated from the grove's medicinal spores — it has healing properties and potent biochemical compounds. Whoever lived here knew what they were doing.

objects.name: Protective Rock Formation
objects.description: A natural rock formation sheltering the grove from the Convergence's direct energy.

then.text: A rock formation shielding the grove from the nearest siphon tower's energy field. Natural stone, dense enough to block the Convergence's drain. This is why the fungi survive here — the rocks create a shadow of protection. A tiny oasis in a dying world.

objects.name: Nutrient Pool
objects.description: A small pool of liquid at the grove's center, fed by fungal runoff.

then.text: A small pool of water collected from fungal runoff. It's clean — the fungi's filtration is natural and effective. The first clean water you've seen on this planet. Drink, rest, and prepare for the journey ahead.

objects.name: Crafting Surface
objects.description: A flat rock surface used as a workbench by a previous survivor.

then.text: A flat rock used as a workbench. Tool marks and stains from previous crafting. This is where the grove's inhabitant worked — combining materials, building tools. A safe place to do the same. The grove provides shelter, light, and a workspace. Everything you need to prepare.

objects.name: Bunker Blast Door
objects.description: A heavy military blast door with alien insignia, partially open.

then.text: A military bunker door, scorched by weapons fire but still standing. The alien military insignia is recognizable — crossed weapons over a shield. The door is partially open, jammed by debris. You can squeeze through. Emergency amber lighting glows from inside.
You squeeze through the gap. The bunker's interior is intact — emergency power still runs. Amber light illuminates a military space: weapons, supplies, records. The last stand of a civilization.

objects.name: Battle Damage
objects.description: Scoring and blast marks on the bunker's exterior from the final battle.

then.text: Blast marks from energy weapons. The bunker was under siege. The defenders held out here, but whatever attacked them eventually breached other sections. These marks tell the story of a desperate last stand. They fought. They lost. But they didn't go quietly.

objects.name: Alien Weapon Locker
objects.description: A military weapons locker, its lock broken open.

then.text: A weapon locker, its lock shattered. Most weapons are gone — taken by defenders in the final battle. One remains: an alien sidearm, compact, designed for four hands but operable with two. Its charge indicator shows partial power.

You take the alien sidearm. It's heavier than it looks. The grip is awkward — designed for wider hands — but the trigger mechanism is simple. The charge indicator shows five shots remaining. Use them wisely.

objects.name: Military Supply Crates
objects.description: Sealed crates of military supplies, rations, and equipment.

then.text: Military supply crates. Some are open and empty — raided by defenders or refugees. Others are sealed. One crate has a radiation warning symbol — it contains monitoring equipment, including radiation badges for working near the siphon towers.
You open the radiation crate. Inside: monitoring equipment and radiation badges. The badges change color when exposed to Convergence energy — a simple but effective safety device.

objects.name: Command Table
objects.description: A tactical table with maps and battle plans.

then.text: The command table. Maps of the city, the wasteland, and the nexus. Battle plans showing attempted assaults on the Convergence's infrastructure. Defense schematics for a weapon — partial, but recognizable. They were building something to fight back. The plans are incomplete, but they show the theoretical framework.

You take the defense schematics. Partial weapon plans — the theoretical framework for turning the Convergence's own energy against it. Combined with the research lab's data in the city, these could complete the weapon design.

objects.name: Communications Equipment
objects.description: Military communications gear, offline but intact.

then.text: Military communications equipment. Offline — the planet's comm network was one of the first things the Convergence destroyed. But the equipment itself is intact. With power, it might be able to reach... something. Someone. If anyone is still listening.

objects.name: Bunker Records Cabinet
objects.description: A cabinet of military records documenting the final defense.

then.text: A records cabinet with the final military communications. Reports of the Convergence's advance, civilian evacuation orders, weapons research updates. And buried in the records — the echo stabilizer prototype. A device that lets you interact safely with the reality Echoes that haunt this world.

You find the echo stabilizer — a small device worn on the wrist. It emits a frequency that stabilizes the Convergence's energy residue around you, allowing safe interaction with the Echoes. With this, the ghostly remnants of this civilization become allies, not hazards.

objects.name: City Gates
objects.description: Massive gates to the dead city, partially collapsed.

then.text: The city gates — massive structures, partially collapsed. The architecture is elegant: sweeping curves, crystalline inlays (now dark), reliefs of the four-armed inhabitants. Through the gap: the dead city. Towers, spires, bridges, all intact. All empty. The gates are big enough to drive a vehicle through. For you, the rubble provides easy access.

With the echo stabilizer active, you pass through the gates. The city's automated defense scanners flicker — they register you as a memory pattern rather than a living intruder. The stabilizer masks your biological signature. The dead city opens before you.

You step through the gates. Immediately, the city's defense grid activates — energy barriers materialize, blocking your path. Automated systems detect living biology and classify you as a threat. You're forced back. You need something to mask your biological signature.

objects.name: Wall Reliefs
objects.description: Carved reliefs depicting tall four-armed figures in the gate walls.

then.text: Carved reliefs of the city's builders — tall, graceful, four-armed. They're depicted in scenes of daily life: working, creating, celebrating. The artistry is exquisite. These people were civilized, creative, alive. The reliefs are their monument, and their epitaph.

objects.name: Dark Crystal Inlays
objects.description: Decorative crystalline inlays in the gate walls, now drained of light.

then.text: Crystal inlays that once glowed with the city's energy grid. Now dark — drained by the Convergence along with everything else. They're the same crystalline technology as the siphon towers, but used for beauty instead of destruction. The same science, different intent.

objects.name: Gate Rubble
objects.description: Rubble from the collapsed section of the gates.

then.text: Rubble from the collapsed gate section. Large enough blocks to hide among, with gaps and crevices throughout. The rubble provides a defensible position with sight lines in both directions.

objects.name: City Beyond the Gates
objects.description: The silent dead city visible through the gate opening.

then.text: Through the gates: the dead city in full. Towers reach toward the sick sky. Bridges arc between buildings. Streets are empty. Lights glow in some windows — automated systems still running, serving a population that no longer exists. Somewhere in there: a library, a research lab, a weapon that could change everything. And something moved. You're sure of it.

objects.name: Gate Mechanism
objects.description: The gate's opening mechanism, damaged but partially functional.

then.text: The gate mechanism — a combination of mechanical and energy-driven systems. Damaged in the battle that collapsed the gate. The mechanical parts could be repaired, but the energy systems are drained. Without power, the gate can't fully open or close.

objects.name: Cliff Edge
objects.description: The edge of a cliff giving a panoramic view of the planet.

then.text: The cliff drops away sharply. Below: more wasteland, stretching to the horizon. The scale of destruction is visible from here — a panoramic view of a dying world. The wind carries dust and the faint hum of siphon beams.

objects.name: Wasteland Panorama
objects.description: The dead wasteland stretching behind you.

then.text: Behind you: the wasteland you crossed. Grey soil, petrified trees, crystal growths. The crashed shuttle is a dark speck in the distance. The fungal grove is a spot of color — the only living thing between here and the crash site. You've come far.

objects.name: City View from Above
objects.description: The ruined city laid out below the overlook.

then.text: The city from above. You can see its layout: a central plaza, residential blocks radiating outward, a temple with a crystalline dome, a power station near the outer wall, and beneath the research district — the weapon vault. The underground railway connects the major districts. From here, you can plan your route.

objects.name: The Nexus
objects.description: The Convergence's nexus — a crystal mountain pulsing with stolen energy.

then.text: The Convergence nexus. A massive crystal mountain, pulsing with the stolen energy of an entire planet. Energy beams from every siphon tower converge on it. The scale is beyond comprehension — a structure that spans kilometers, driven deep into the planet's core. This is the enemy. This is what you have to destroy. Or understand. Or become. The choice comes later. For now, you need to reach it alive.

objects.name: Converging Energy Beams
objects.description: Dozens of energy siphon beams converging on the distant nexus.

then.text: Energy beams from across the planet, converging on the nexus. Each one represents a siphon tower draining a section of the world. From here, you can count dozens — and there are more beyond the horizon. The planet's entire energy output, channeled to one point. An apocalypse rendered in light.

objects.name: Carved Overlook Marker
objects.description: An ancient marker stone at the overlook, carved by the planet's inhabitants.

then.text: A marker stone, ancient, carved long before the Convergence came. The inscription — if you could read it — probably named this overlook. A place where people came to see their world. To admire it. To show their children. Now it overlooks the end of everything.

objects.name: Flickering Ghost Buildings
objects.description: Translucent buildings flickering in and out of existence.

then.text: Buildings flicker in and out — ghostly, translucent. They're memories burned into the Convergence's energy field: the city as it was, overlapping with the barren wasteland as it is. For a moment, you see a street alive with four-armed figures. Then they're gone. Then they're back. Reality stutters like a broken recording.

objects.name: Echo Manifestations
objects.description: Ghostly alien figures replaying their final moments.

then.text: Ghostly figures — the Echoes. They replay their final moments: a family running, a soldier firing at nothing, a child looking up at the sky. They don't see you. They're trapped in their last moments, preserved in energy like insects in amber. Without the echo stabilizer, they're just images. With it, some might be reached.

With the stabilizer active, you reach out to an Echo — a scientist, running with data crystals clutched in four hands. The Echo flickers, and for a moment, sees you. 'You... you're alive? How? Take this path — it leads to the bunker. They stored the weapon plans there. Hurry. The Watcher is coming.' The Echo points, then dissolves.

You call out to the Echoes. They don't react. They're not really here — just energy patterns, playing back. Without some way to stabilize the field, you can't interact with them. They loop, and loop, and loop.

objects.name: Reality Boundary
objects.description: The shimmering edge where normal reality meets the echo field.

then.text: The boundary shimmers — a visible line where normal reality meets the echo field. Cross it, and the world flickers between past and present. The boundary crackles with energy, dangerous to touch. It marks the edge of the Convergence's energy saturation zone.

objects.name: Ghost Vehicle
objects.description: A translucent alien vehicle, frozen mid-flight in the echo field.

then.text: An alien vehicle, frozen mid-flight in the echo field. It's translucent, ghostly — an energy echo of the real vehicle that once traveled this road. You can see inside: empty seats designed for four-armed occupants. It was heading away from the city. Fleeing.

objects.name: Stable Ground Patch
objects.description: A section of ground where reality is more stable, safe to stand on.

then.text: A patch of stable ground — here, reality holds firm. The echo field flickers around you, but this spot is anchored. Safe to rest, safe to plan. The stable patches form a path through the field, if you navigate carefully.

objects.name: Time Distortion Zone
objects.description: An area where time itself stutters and loops.

then.text: Time stutters here. You see the same dust mote fall, rise, and fall again. Shadows jump backward. Sound echoes before it's made. The Convergence's energy has fractured the local timestream. Moving through this zone would be disorienting and dangerous without protection. The echo stabilizer might help.

objects.name: Dry Fountain
objects.description: An ornamental fountain, bone-dry. The basin is cracked.

then.text: A grand fountain, now dry. The basin is cracked and filled with dust. Water channels lead to it from all directions — once this was the heart of the plaza. Coins or their alien equivalent litter the bottom.
You reach into the dry basin and sift through the dust. Your fingers find nothing of use — just faded tokens and crumbled offerings.

objects.name: Four-Armed Statue
objects.description: A towering statue of one of the planet's former inhabitants.

then.text: A tall, four-armed figure carved from pale stone. Its expression is serene, its upper arms raised in a gesture of welcome. Around its neck hangs a carved pendant — the same symbol you've seen on the library and temple. At the base, an inscription in alien script.
The inscription reads: 'We who remain welcome those who come after. Take the keystone. Remember us.' The statue's lower right hand holds a removable stone token.
You pry the stone token from the statue's hand. It's warm to the touch — a city keystone, granting access to restricted areas.

You run your hands over the stone base. The carving is exquisite — four arms in perfect proportion. The lower right hand seems to grip something, but you can't tell what without understanding the inscription.

objects.name: Abandoned Table
objects.description: A dining table with a meal still set. The food has long since petrified.

then.text: A meal for three, frozen in time. Alien cutlery laid out — wide-handled, designed for four-armed diners. The food is petrified, grey. A drinking vessel is tipped over, its contents long evaporated. They were mid-meal when the evacuation order came.
You duck under the table. It's large enough to hide beneath, though the legs leave you partially visible.

objects.name: Stopped Vehicle
objects.description: An alien ground transport, stopped mid-road.

then.text: A sleek ground transport — no wheels, hovering on dead repulsors an inch above the road surface. The canopy is open. Personal belongings on the passenger platform: a satchel, data crystals, what might be children's drawings on alien paper. The driver left in a hurry.
You climb into the vehicle's cargo space. It's cramped but hidden from view. The repulsors hum faintly — there's still residual power.

objects.name: City Map Kiosk
objects.description: A public information terminal showing a city map.

then.text: A public kiosk with a holographic city map still flickering. Districts are labeled in alien script. You can make out major landmarks by their icons — a book symbol (library), crossed weapons (war room), a gear (power station), a crystal spire (temple). The underground railway connects them all.
You tap the holographic interface. The map zooms and rotates, showing you building interiors, transit routes, and — most importantly — the path from the underground railway to the research district.

objects.name: Flickering Echo
objects.description: A translucent figure materializes near the fountain.

then.text: A tall, four-armed figure shimmers into view. It's translucent, ghostly — wearing what looks like civilian clothing. It turns slowly, as if searching for someone. Its mouth moves but no sound comes. This Echo is more coherent than the ones in the wasteland.

The Echo's voice comes through the communicator, thin and distorted: "You... you're not one of us. But you're here. The library — go to the library. Our scientists left everything there. The cipher, the research, the warnings. Hurry. The crystal watcher sees all."

The stabilizer hums. The Echo solidifies slightly, enough to gesture. It points firmly toward the library district, then toward the underground. It mimes running. The message is clear: go, and go fast.
"Hello?" The Echo doesn't respond. It continues its loop — turning, searching, mouthing silent words. Without the right equipment, you can't bridge the gap.

objects.name: Plaza Archway
objects.description: An arched bridge connecting buildings above the plaza.

then.text: Graceful arched bridges connect the buildings surrounding the plaza, three stories up. The architecture is beautiful — sweeping curves, no sharp edges, everything flowing into everything else. Lights still glow in some of the windows above.

objects.name: City Spire
objects.description: One of the city's tall crystalline spires rises from the plaza's edge.

then.text: A crystalline spire rises from the plaza's edge, tapering to a point high above. Its surface is etched with geometric patterns that may be decorative or functional — perhaps both. At its base, a door-shaped panel is sealed with a keystone lock.
The keystone slots into the lock. The panel slides open silently, revealing an interior staircase spiraling upward. From above: a view of the entire city and, in the distance, the nexus.

objects.name: Data Crystal Stacks
objects.description: Floor-to-ceiling racks of glowing data crystals.

then.text: Thousands of data crystals in precisely labeled slots, floor to ceiling. The format is identical to the Choir's archive on the ship — the Choir copied this civilization's storage technology. Or stole it. Most crystals glow faintly blue. One section glows amber — marked with a warning symbol.
You squeeze between the stacks. The rows are narrow but tall — perfect cover for someone your size. The crystals hum softly around you.

With full power restored, the crystal stacks light up completely. An automated retrieval system activates, presenting crystals to your reading station based on your searches. The library is fully operational.

objects.name: Reading Station
objects.description: A data crystal reader with a holographic display.

then.text: A reading station with a crystal slot and a holographic projector. The projector flickers with residual power. A crystal is already loaded — someone was mid-research when the evacuation hit.

You activate the loaded crystal. A holographic display sputters to life — alien text scrolls past, accompanied by diagrams. Without the translation cipher, you can only make out a few words: 'convergence,' 'harvest,' 'weapon,' 'failure.'

With the cipher, the text becomes clear: a research report on the Convergence's energy harvesting method and the civilization's countermeasure theory. The energy can be turned back on itself — but the weapon was never fully assembled. The components were scattered across secured vaults.

objects.name: Holographic Index
objects.description: A library catalog system with a shimmering holographic interface.

then.text: A holographic catalog, still operational. Symbols float in the air — categories, subjects, locations. One section is highlighted in urgent red, labeled with the Convergence warning symbol. The last search query is still active: it translated roughly to 'countermeasure status.'
You navigate the index, searching for translation aids. The system presents a crystal from the linguistics section — glowing differently from the others. You pull it from the retrieval slot.
Translation Cipher Fragment 4 of 4 obtained. With all four fragments, you can assemble the complete cipher.

objects.name: Convergence Research Section
objects.description: A restricted section of the library dedicated to studying the Convergence threat.

then.text: A sealed section marked with warning symbols. Through the transparent barrier you can see data crystals glowing an angry red — the civilization's research on the Convergence. A keystone lock secures the entrance.

The keystone opens the restricted section. Inside: decades of research on the Convergence. Energy patterns, planetary consumption rates, weakness analyses. And one crystal labeled in urgent script — the weapon schematics overview.
The barrier holds firm. A keystone lock requires the city's access token. This section was restricted even before the evacuation.

objects.name: Study Alcove
objects.description: A small reading alcove between the stacks.

then.text: A cozy reading alcove, built for a four-armed reader who could hold two crystals at once while taking notes with two free hands. A cushioned bench, a small reading lamp. Untouched since the evacuation.
You curl up in the alcove, pulling the cushion over you. From outside, you'd look like an oddly-shaped pillow.

objects.name: Holographic Tactical Table
objects.description: A massive table projecting a 3D map of the planet.

then.text: A massive tactical table, dark. Its surface is embedded with thousands of tiny projectors. Labels around the edge — unit designations, defense grid sectors, emergency protocols. All offline. The power station could change that.

The table blazes to life. A 3D hologram of the planet rotates above it, covered in red markers — every siphon tower, every energy conduit, every harvesting node. The defense grid overlay shows orbital satellite positions, all marked OFFLINE. A controller module sits in a locked drawer beneath the table.

You pull open the drawer beneath the table. Inside: the defense grid controller — the interface for the orbital satellite network. With enough power, this could reactivate the planet's last line of defense.
Dead. The table needs external power. The city's power station might still be restorable.

objects.name: Tactical Displays
objects.description: Wall-mounted screens showing battle plans.

then.text: Tactical screens on the walls, some still dimly lit by backup power. Battle formations, retreat routes, civilian evacuation plans. The final entries show a desperate assault plan — a strike team heading into the Convergence nexus itself. The team's route is marked: through the underground railway, under the city, into the crystal heart. They never came back.

objects.name: Communications Array
objects.description: Military communication equipment, some still powered.

then.text: Military-grade communication equipment. Most channels are dead, but the backup power feeds a few receivers. Static hisses from speakers. The last logged transmission, timestamped to the final day: 'Strike team has entered the nexus. All units fall back to evacuation points. May the resonance carry us home.'

You scan through frequencies. Dead. Dead. Static. Dead. Then — a faint rhythmic pulse. Not a voice. Not a signal. A heartbeat. The Convergence's energy has a rhythm, and it's broadcasting on every frequency.

objects.name: Battle Plans
objects.description: Printed tactical documents spread across a secondary table.

then.text: With the cipher, the battle plans reveal everything: the nexus assault route, the weapon assembly location inside the nexus, the escape shaft the team carved as a fallback. They knew exactly what they were doing. They just didn't have enough time to finish the weapon.

Physical documents — alien paper with dense tactical writing and diagrams. You can make out the nexus structure in cross-section, arrows showing an assault path, and what looks like a weapon schematic. Without the translation cipher, the details are lost.

objects.name: Equipment Locker
objects.description: A military storage locker, partially open.

then.text: A military equipment locker, door hanging open. Most contents were taken during the evacuation — empty weapon racks, cleared shelves. But a few items remain: emergency rations (long expired), a damaged comm device, and a personal locket wedged behind a shelf.
You squeeze inside the locker. It's dark and cramped but provides good cover.

objects.name: Commander's Chair
objects.description: A large chair at the head of the tactical table.

then.text: A command chair, designed for a four-armed occupant. The armrests are worn smooth from years of use. Whoever sat here made the hardest decisions of the war. On the seat: a folded cloth — a personal standard or flag, left behind when the last commander vacated.

objects.name: Prototype Weapon
objects.description: An incomplete energy weapon on a central platform.

then.text: A partially assembled energy weapon on a containment platform. Crystalline components fused with metal framework. It's elegant — designed to channel and redirect Convergence energy back at its source. But key components are missing: the core, the dampener, the focusing crystal. The assembly was abandoned mid-work.
The prototype is fused to its platform — it can't be moved. But studying it gives you insight into how the components fit together. This is a reference model, not the weapon itself.

objects.name: Research Workstation
objects.description: A scientist's workstation with active holographic schematics.

then.text: A research workstation, holographic displays still active on minimal power. Weapon schematics hover in the air — detailed cross-sections of the countermeasure device. Notes in alien script surround the diagrams.

With the cipher, the schematics become clear: assembly instructions for the countermeasure. Weapon core seats into the resonance crystal housing. Energy dampener wraps the assembly. Siphon crystal fragment provides the ignition charge. You memorize the sequence.
You manipulate the holographic displays but can't read the annotations. The diagrams alone show component shapes and positions, but without translation you're guessing at the assembly order.

objects.name: Weapon Schematics
objects.description: Detailed holographic schematics of the countermeasure device.

then.text: Floating holographic weapon schematics. The design is elegant: a three-component device that captures, reverses, and amplifies the Convergence's own energy. The theory is sound — the execution was what failed. They ran out of time.
You can't take a hologram. But the workstation has a portable data crystal reader — you download the schematics to a blank crystal.

objects.name: Energy Containment Field
objects.description: A shimmering field containing raw Convergence energy samples.

then.text: A containment field holding samples of raw Convergence energy. The energy pulses and writhes inside the field like a living thing. This is what the scientists were studying — the enemy's blood, captured and contained.
You reach toward the field and snatch your hand back — the air around it burns with static electricity. The field is holding but deteriorating. Touching it unprotected would be lethal.

objects.name: Equipment Rack
objects.description: Scientific instruments and protective equipment.

then.text: Racks of scientific equipment: energy meters, calibration tools, safety equipment. Most are sized for four-armed users, but a pair of goggles and some smaller instruments might work for you.
You take a pair of safety goggles. They're oversized but adjustable — you tighten the strap to fit. These should protect against energy flashes in the nexus.

objects.name: Supply Cabinet
objects.description: A tall cabinet with lab supplies.

then.text: A tall supply cabinet with sliding doors. Large enough to hide inside, with ventilation slits that would let you see out.
You slide open the cabinet and climb inside, pulling the door almost shut behind you. Through the ventilation slits, you can watch the lab without being seen.

objects.name: Open Doorway
objects.description: An open doorway into an alien home.

then.text: An open doorway into someone's home. Inside: curved furniture designed for four-armed beings, a low table with an unfinished game, artwork on the walls showing landscapes that no longer exist. It's heartbreakingly ordinary. Someone lived here. Loved here. Left everything behind.
You slip inside the home and crouch behind the curved sofa. The furniture is oversized for you — perfect cover. Through the window you can watch the street.

objects.name: Children's Toys
objects.description: Alien toys scattered on the floor of a home.

then.text: Toys scattered on the floor. Four-armed action figures. Building blocks with alien geometry. A stuffed creature that might be this world's equivalent of a teddy bear. A child was playing here when the evacuation was called. The toys are still warm — not literally, but they hold the warmth of normalcy. This is the hardest thing you've seen yet.

objects.name: Packed Luggage
objects.description: Hastily packed bags left in a doorway.

then.text: Bags packed in a hurry — clothes spilling out, a data crystal reader shoved in sideways, alien identification documents. They were planning to evacuate. They packed. They never left.

You search through the luggage. Personal effects, clothing sized for four-armed beings, preserved food packets (long expired). Nothing useful... wait. Tucked in a side pocket: a small personal locket, the kind worn around the neck.

objects.name: Family Portraits
objects.description: A wall of alien family photographs.

then.text: Family portraits on the wall. The alien equivalent of photographs — holographic captures frozen in crystal frames. A family of four — two adults, two children. All four-armed, all smiling in their alien way. The children are playing. The adults watch with what can only be love. This species was not so different from yours.

objects.name: Residential Echo
objects.description: A ghostly figure appears in the doorway of a home.

then.text: An Echo — a tall figure in a doorway, looking back into a home that no longer exists as they remember it. This one is more coherent than most. Their four arms hang at their sides. Their face shows something universal: grief.

You hold up the locket. The Echo SEES it. Its form solidifies, its expression shifting from grief to recognition. Through the communicator: "That was... mine. My family. I couldn't... we couldn't get out in time. The children..." A long silence. "The temple. Go to the temple. The prophecy speaks of one who comes after. That's you. Take the prophet's crystal. It will show you the way."
Through the communicator: "Who are you? You're so small. Are you... from the specimens? They took you too? I'm sorry. I'm so sorry for everything." The Echo flickers. It's losing coherence.
You speak softly. The Echo doesn't respond — it can't hear you without the right equipment. It continues its silent vigil in the doorway.

objects.name: Abandoned Meal
objects.description: A meal for one, left on a kitchen counter.

then.text: A single serving of alien food on a counter. The food has petrified into grey stone. A beverage glass, half-empty. Someone was eating alone when the world ended. They didn't even finish their drink.

objects.name: Reactor Chamber
objects.description: The city's main power reactor, partially operational.

then.text: The city's main reactor — a large cylindrical chamber with energy cores that glow faintly. It's on standby power: enough for emergency systems but not the full grid. The engineering is impressive — robust, built to last millennia. And it has, mostly.

Too high to reach. The reactor controls are at full-height alien console level. But the adapter bridges technologies — you connect it to a low-level maintenance port and route power from the adapter's reserves to jump-start the reactor.

objects.name: Power Distribution Panel
objects.description: Controls for routing power to different city districts.

then.text: A power distribution panel — toggle switches for each city district. Currently all offline. Labels identify each district: library, temple, war room, research, residential, railway, and — ominously — 'deep transit' leading down toward the nexus.

With the reactor running, the panel comes alive. But the gauges show limited power — you can only activate 3 of 7 districts. Choose carefully: each district you power up reveals new interactions and resources, but also makes that area visible to The Watcher.
Dead switches. Without the reactor running, there's nothing to distribute.

objects.name: Backup Systems
objects.description: Emergency backup power units along the wall.

then.text: Emergency backup units — these are what's been keeping the city's minimal systems running for millennia. Status indicators show most at 2-5% capacity. One unit is at 15% — relatively fresh. A power cell adapter port is visible on each unit.
You find a universal power cell adapter mounted on the side of the freshest backup unit. This bridges alien and human technology — it could interface with anything.

objects.name: Convergence Breach
objects.description: Crystalline growths pushing through the station wall.

then.text: Crystalline Convergence growths have breached the station wall, pushing through concrete and metal like roots through soil. The crystals pulse with stolen energy. This is how the Convergence spreads — it literally grows through infrastructure, consuming and converting.
The crystals are razor-sharp and thrumming with energy. Touching them would be extremely dangerous. But they're warm — warm with the stolen life of a planet.

objects.name: Power Conduits
objects.description: Thick energy conduits running between the reactor and the distribution panel.

then.text: Heavy power conduits connecting the reactor to the distribution panel. They're dark now, but you can see where they branch off to feed each city district. Robust engineering — minimal damage despite millennia of neglect.

objects.name: Maintenance Hatch
objects.description: A floor-level maintenance hatch.

then.text: A floor-level maintenance hatch. It's sized for maintenance drones, not full-sized workers — but it's perfect for someone your size. Leads to the conduit tunnels beneath the station.
You pull the hatch open and drop into the narrow maintenance tunnel beneath. It's cramped but completely hidden from above.

objects.name: Resonance Chamber
objects.description: A circular depression in the temple floor that glows with energy.

then.text: A circular depression in the floor, lined with crystalline material that glows faintly. This is where the inhabitants communed through vibration — a species that spoke through subsonic resonance, like the Choir but natural. The chamber still resonates when you step near it.

You strike the tuning fork and hold it over the chamber. The crystal lining SINGS — a deep, beautiful tone that fills the temple. Echoes manifest around you, dozens of them, a congregation of the dead. For one moment, the temple is alive again. Then the resonance fades, and they fade with it. But the chamber's energy has unlocked something at the altar.

You step into the chamber. The crystal hums around you, responding to your presence. Faint vibrations travel through your bones. But without the right frequency, you can't activate the full resonance.

objects.name: Temple Altar
objects.description: A stone altar with alien offerings.

then.text: A stone altar with offerings: dried alien flowers, crystalline tokens, small figurines of the four-armed species. A sealed compartment in the altar's base bears the temple's resonance symbol. Above it, an inscription you can barely make out.

The resonance has unsealed the altar compartment. Inside: a crystal unlike any you've seen — perfectly clear, with swirling patterns of light inside that seem to show... images. Possible futures. The prophet's crystal.
The altar compartment is sealed — the resonance lock holds firm. The temple's resonance chamber might hold the key.
Among the offerings, you find a resonance tuning fork — a crystalline instrument used in the species' meditation practices. It hums when you touch it.

objects.name: Temple Murals
objects.description: Wall paintings depicting the species' history and prophecy.

then.text: Murals covering the walls, painted in pigments that still glow after millennia. They tell a story: the species rising from simple beginnings, building cities, reaching the stars. A golden age. Then darkness — a crystalline force arriving from deep space. The final panels show a small figure — tiny compared to the four-armed inhabitants — standing before a great crystal. The prophecy of 'the one who comes after.'

With the cipher, the inscriptions beneath each mural become clear. The prophecy reads: 'When the crystal consumes the last light, one will come from the specimens. Small of body, vast of will. They will carry what we could not finish. They will face the heart of the crystal. They will choose.' The murals show six possible endings — six paths the 'small one' might take. Some end in light. Some in darkness. All end in choice.

objects.name: Offerings
objects.description: Small offerings left by worshippers.

then.text: Small personal offerings: crystalline tokens, tiny figurines, pressed alien flowers. Each one represents a prayer, a hope, a farewell. The last offerings were desperate — hastily placed, some still clutched by ghost-hands that have long since faded.

objects.name: Crystal Walls
objects.description: The temple's crystalline walls filter light beautifully.

then.text: The temple walls are grown from living crystal — or were, once. The crystal is dead now, but it still filters light beautifully, casting prismatic patterns across the floor. The craftsmanship is stunning — this species built with crystal the way humans build with glass.

objects.name: Meditation Alcove
objects.description: A small alcove for private meditation.

then.text: A small alcove for private meditation, with a cushioned seat and a crystal resonance panel on the back wall. Intimate, quiet, sheltered from view.
You slip into the alcove and pull the crystal curtain across. In the dim crystalline light, you're nearly invisible.

objects.name: Rail Vehicle
objects.description: An alien transit vehicle stopped on the tracks.

then.text: A sleek transit vehicle on magnetic rails, stopped mid-journey. The doors are open. Inside: seating for about twenty four-armed passengers. Emergency lighting strips glow amber along the ceiling. The control console at the front still has power — a token reader waits for a railway pass.

You insert the token into the reader. The vehicle hums to life — magnetic rails engaging, doors cycling. The destination board lights up with station names. Fast travel through the city is now possible.
You climb aboard and duck between the seats. Good cover from anything outside, though the open doors leave you somewhat exposed.

objects.name: Railway Platform
objects.description: The transit platform with benches and a token dispenser.

then.text: A transit platform with benches and a token dispenser. The dispenser's display reads something in alien script. A few tokens are scattered on the ground — dropped during the evacuation rush.
You pick up a transit token from the platform floor. It's warm, made from compressed crystalline material with magnetic properties. Should work in any rail vehicle's reader.

objects.name: Survivor Markings
objects.description: Desperate messages scratched into the tunnel walls.

then.text: Scratched messages in the tunnel walls. Even without the cipher, some are clear from context: arrows pointing to safe areas, X marks for dangers, crude maps of the tunnel system. Survivors hid here, used the tunnels to move through the city unseen.

With the cipher: 'The crystal watcher patrols above — stay underground.' 'Food cache at junction 7.' 'The deep tunnel leads to the nexus. DON'T GO THAT WAY.' 'If anyone finds this — we went to the bunker. All of us. May the resonance carry us.'

objects.name: Flooded Section
objects.description: A section of tunnel partially flooded with stagnant water.

then.text: A section of tunnel flooded with stagnant water — a broken pipe from above. The water is knee-deep for you. Stepping through it would be noisy, but going around means a much longer route.

You wade through the cold water. It splashes with every step, echoing through the tunnel. Your size is actually helpful here — the water only reaches your waist where it would barely cover a local's ankles.

objects.name: Railway Controls
objects.description: A junction control box for switching tracks.

then.text: A junction control box — switches tracks to route vehicles to different stations. The labels list destinations including a final unlabeled route that leads downward. The deep transit tunnel to the nexus.

You throw the switch to the deep transit route. The rails hum as they realign. The path to the nexus is open — but it's a one-way trip. The tunnel descends beneath the city into the planet's crust. Point of no return.

objects.name: Deep Tunnel
objects.description: The tunnel stretches into darkness in both directions.

then.text: The tunnel stretches into total darkness. Emergency lights are spaced far apart, creating pools of amber in the blackness. You can feel a draft — the tunnel is connected to vast spaces deeper underground. The nexus is down there.
You press yourself into a maintenance alcove in the tunnel wall. In the darkness, you're invisible.

objects.name: Reality Boundary
objects.description: The shimmering barrier between past and present.

then.text: A vertical shimmer runs through the center of the room — the boundary between two realities. On one side: the ruined present, crumbling and dark. On the other: the living past, bright and functional. The boundary crackles with energy and shifts unpredictably.

The stabilizer lets you push through the boundary without being torn apart. Reality warps around you — for a disorienting moment you exist in both times simultaneously. Then you step through into the past-echo version of the room.
You reach toward the boundary and jerk your hand back — your fingers went translucent, caught between times. Without stabilization, crossing this could erase you.

objects.name: Ruined Present
objects.description: The decayed, present-day version of the room.

then.text: The ruined half — walls crumbling, consoles dark and dead, dust thick on every surface. This is reality: millennia of decay, the Convergence's slow drain. Rubble provides cover but nothing of use.
You duck behind a collapsed wall section. The rubble makes decent cover in the ruined half.

objects.name: Living Past
objects.description: The pristine, past-echo version of the room.

then.text: The living past — the same room as it was, pristine and operational. Screens glow with data. The air is warm and clean. It's beautiful and wrong — you're seeing a moment that ended millennia ago, preserved in the Convergence's energy like a fly in amber.

In the past-echo, the consoles are functional. You access the screens — they show the last day's data: evacuation orders, weapon status reports, and a final transmission from the strike team entering the nexus. A key revelation: the weapon was completed but not assembled. The components were separated and stored in the vault.

objects.name: Ghost Scientist
objects.description: A translucent four-armed figure at a console.

then.text: A ghostly scientist — translucent, four-armed, wearing a lab coat. They repeat the same actions: checking screens, making notes, looking toward the door with increasing urgency. Their loop is the last moments before evacuation. They didn't want to leave their work.

Through the communicator: "The weapon... it's finished. The components are in the vault. Biometric locks — they were afraid someone would use it prematurely. But there's a bypass... the neural tendril interface... combined with the stabilizer and an adapter, it mimics our biology close enough. I left notes in the research lab. Please... finish what we started."
The ghost doesn't respond to your voice. It continues its loop — checking, noting, looking at the door. If only you could reach it.

objects.name: Past-Echo Console
objects.description: A console that exists only in the echo of the past.

then.text: A console that exists in the past-echo half of the room. In the present, this space holds only rubble. The screen shows rapidly scrolling data — research outputs, energy calculations, weapon specifications.

You interact with the past-echo console. It responds to your touch — in this preserved moment, everything is real. You download the final research data to a portable crystal. This includes the complete weapon assembly sequence and the vault access bypass protocol.

objects.name: Shimmering Crack
objects.description: A crack in reality where the boundary is weakest.

then.text: A crack in the reality boundary, widening slowly. Through it you can see both times simultaneously — the ruined present and the living past overlapping in nauseating double-vision. The Convergence's energy is destabilizing local spacetime. This won't hold forever.

objects.name: Containment Units
objects.description: Separate sealed units holding weapon components.

then.text: Separate containment units along the walls, each behind energy barriers and biometric locks. Each unit holds a different weapon component — scattered and secured so that no single breach could compromise the whole weapon. The barriers still hum with power.
The energy barrier stings your palm. The biometric lock scans your hand and rejects it — wrong species. You need a way to fool the biometric system.

objects.name: Biometric Lock
objects.description: An alien biometric scanner keyed to four-armed physiology.

then.text: A sophisticated biometric scanner. It reads neural patterns, body temperature, and limb configuration. Designed to recognize only authorized members of the four-armed species. You need to trick it into accepting you as a valid match.

You connect the neural tendril to the stabilizer's signal processor and route it through the power adapter. The jury-rigged interface mimics the neural pattern of a four-armed species close enough to fool the ancient scanner. The biometric lock clicks. The energy barriers drop.
The scanner rejects you again. You need a way to present the right biological signature — something that carries the species' neural pattern.

objects.name: Weapon Pedestal
objects.description: A central pedestal where the assembled weapon was meant to sit.

then.text: A central pedestal with a weapon mount — the place where the assembled countermeasure was meant to sit. Empty. The mount has three slots: one for the weapon core, one for the dampener, one for the focusing crystal. This is where it would have been assembled.
With the vault open, you can retrieve the weapon core from its containment unit. It's heavy for your size but manageable. The core pulses with latent energy.

objects.name: Energy Barriers
objects.description: Glowing barriers protecting each containment unit.

then.text: Shimmering energy barriers — each one protecting a weapon component. The barriers are powered by the vault's own internal reactor. They've held for millennia and show no signs of weakening.
The barriers have dropped. The containment units stand open, their treasures accessible. After millennia of protection, the weapon components are finally within reach.

objects.name: Vault Security Door
objects.description: The heavy door to the weapon vault.

then.text: A massive security door, already open — forced by the strike team during their assault. Blast marks around the frame show it wasn't easy. Beyond: the research lab above, or deeper into the vault.

objects.name: Forced Containment Unit
objects.description: One containment unit has been forced open — empty.

then.text: One containment unit was forced open — probably by the strike team. It's empty. Whatever was inside was taken to the nexus and never returned. The interior is large enough to hide in.
You climb into the empty containment unit and pull the door mostly shut. The interior is padded and shielded — perfect hiding spot.

objects.name: Crystallized Ground
objects.description: The soil has been transformed into pure crystal.

then.text: The ground itself has crystallized — soil, rock, and everything in it transformed into transparent crystal by the Convergence's energy. You can see layers of geological strata frozen in crystal. Deep below, energy veins pulse with stolen life.

objects.name: Frozen Trees
objects.description: Alien trees frozen mid-growth in transparent crystal.

then.text: Trees caught mid-growth, encased in crystal. You can see every branch, every leaf, perfectly preserved. Some were flowering when the energy wave hit. They're beautiful — frozen beauty, the Convergence's inadvertent art.
You squeeze between the crystal trunks. They're close enough together to provide decent cover, and the crystal refracts light in confusing patterns.

objects.name: Energy Veins
objects.description: Glowing veins of stolen energy flowing through the ground.

then.text: Veins of pure energy flowing through the crystallized ground, visible through the transparent surface. They pulse rhythmically — the planet's stolen life being pumped toward the nexus. The light they cast is cold and blue.

objects.name: Nexus Vista
objects.description: The massive crystal nexus dominates the horizon.

then.text: The nexus fills the sky — a crystal mountain pulsing with stolen energy, energy beams from across the planet converging on its peak. It's awe-inspiring and terrifying. The air vibrates with power. Reality itself seems to warp near it, the sky turning from yellow-green to white.

objects.name: Crystal Formation
objects.description: A cluster of Convergence crystals growing from the ground.

then.text: A cluster of Convergence crystals, still actively growing. You can see them inch forward in real-time, consuming the ground. The crystals crackle with energy and radiate heat.
The dampener suppresses the crystal's energy. It stops growing, dims, and cracks. A path through the crystal field opens briefly.

objects.name: Warped Air
objects.description: The air shimmers and distorts near the nexus.

then.text: The air warps and distorts. Light bends wrong. For a moment you see double — the landscape as it is and as it was, overlapping. The Convergence's energy is so concentrated here that spacetime itself is unstable.

objects.name: Nexus Entrance
objects.description: The massive opening at the base of the nexus.

then.text: The entrance to the nexus — a gargantuan opening in the crystal base, large enough to fly a shuttle through. The walls are pure energy made solid, glowing with blinding intensity. A tunnel descends into the planet's depths. The hum is deafening. Once you enter, there's no guarantee you can come back.
You step through the entrance. The energy washes over you — warm, tingling, alive. The tunnel descends steeply. Behind you, the daylight fades. Ahead, only crystal light.

objects.name: Crystal Walls
objects.description: Walls of pure crystallized energy.

then.text: Walls of pure crystallized energy. Not built — grown, over eons. The crystal is warm to the touch and vibrates with the nexus's power. Faint patterns move through it like thoughts through a brain.

objects.name: Energy Pulses
objects.description: Visible energy pulses traveling through the nexus structure.

then.text: Energy pulses travel visibly through the crystal structure — like blood through veins, or data through fiber optics. Each pulse carries stolen planetary energy toward the core. The rhythm is steady: pump, pause, pump, pause. Like a heartbeat.

objects.name: Descent Tunnel
objects.description: The tunnel descending into the planet's depths.

then.text: The tunnel angles downward steeply. You can see tool marks on the crystal walls — the strike team carved handholds and steps during their assault. The crystal grows back slowly, partially covering their work.

objects.name: Ancient Markings
objects.description: Markings older than the planet's civilization.

then.text: Markings etched into the crystal that predate the planet's civilization by billions of years. The Convergence — or whatever built the nexus — left these. They're not language. They're energy patterns frozen in crystal. Mathematical. Beautiful. Incomprehensible.

objects.name: Energy Rivers
objects.description: Massive conduits of flowing stolen energy.

then.text: Rivers of pure energy flow through crystalline conduits — the stolen life force of an entire planet, compressed and channeled toward the core. The light is almost too bright to look at directly. The heat is intense. Without protection, prolonged exposure would be lethal.

objects.name: Metal Walkway
objects.description: A narrow walkway built by the former civilization.

then.text: A narrow metal walkway spanning between the energy conduits — built by the strike team during their assault on the nexus. It's bolted into the crystal walls with alien engineering. Stable enough, but terrifyingly exposed above rivers of energy.

objects.name: Conduit Junction
objects.description: Where multiple energy conduits converge.

then.text: A junction where three energy conduits merge into one larger flow. The energy pulses sync here, creating a brief gap between surges. With precise timing, you could cross.
You watch the pulse pattern... wait for the gap... and dash across. The goggles protect your eyes from the blinding flash as the next pulse surges past, inches from your back.
The energy is blinding without eye protection. You can't time your crossing if you can't see the pulse patterns.

objects.name: Energy Tap
objects.description: A point where raw Convergence energy can be sampled.

then.text: A maintenance tap on the conduit — the strike team installed it to study the energy flow. A small sample could be extracted here, though handling raw Convergence energy is incredibly dangerous.

Using the dampener to suppress the energy's intensity, you carefully extract a small sample into a containment vial. The energy writhes inside, alive and furious. Pure Convergence energy — the most dangerous substance you've ever held.
You reach for the tap and immediately recoil — the energy singes your fingers even at a distance. You need something to suppress the energy intensity before handling it.

objects.name: Heat Shimmer
objects.description: Waves of intense heat rising from the energy conduits.

then.text: Waves of heat rise from the energy conduits, distorting the air. The temperature here is extreme — the energy of a planet compressed into flowing rivers. The walkways stay cooler thanks to alien thermal shielding, but step off them and you'd cook in seconds.

objects.name: Walkway Railing
objects.description: A simple railing along the walkway edge.

then.text: A simple metal railing. Below: rivers of energy that would vaporize you. The railing is the only thing between you and oblivion. It's not very tall.

objects.name: Harvesting Apparatus
objects.description: The massive machine that drains the planet.

then.text: The harvesting apparatus — a massive structure of crystal and dark unknown matter. Energy rivers flow into it from every direction, compressed into a single beam that fires upward through the nexus into space. This is the machine that kills planets. It's ancient, alien, and terrifyingly beautiful. The sound it makes is like a choir singing in frequencies that hurt.

You place the countermeasure at the apparatus's energy intake. The weapon activates — channeling the Convergence's own energy back on itself. The apparatus shudders. The beam wavers. Crystal cracks spread from the contact point. The machine that kills planets is dying.

objects.name: Energy Beam
objects.description: A concentrated beam of stolen energy firing into space.

then.text: A beam of compressed planetary energy, impossibly bright, firing straight up through the nexus into orbit and beyond. This is the Convergence's pipeline — stolen life force transmitted to the greater entity somewhere in deep space. The beam crackles and roars.

objects.name: Crystal Cathedral
objects.description: Crystal formations surrounding the apparatus like a cathedral.

then.text: Natural crystal formations rising around the apparatus like the pillars of a cathedral. They amplify and direct the energy flow. Some are large enough to hide behind — if you can tolerate the vibration.
You press yourself against the base of a crystal pillar. The vibration rattles your teeth, but the crystal's refractive properties make you nearly invisible in the ambient light.

objects.name: Apparatus Base
objects.description: The base of the harvesting machine, where components can be accessed.

then.text: The base of the apparatus — where energy inputs connect. Access panels and maintenance ports are visible, some pried open by the strike team. This is where the countermeasure would need to be placed to reverse the energy flow.

objects.name: Countermeasure Slot
objects.description: A slot at the apparatus base where the countermeasure fits.

then.text: An access point at the base of the apparatus — shaped to accept the countermeasure weapon. The strike team created this interface before they were overwhelmed. The slot leads directly to the apparatus's energy intake.

objects.name: Choir Consoles
objects.description: Bio-organic Choir technology layered over ancient controls.

then.text: Choir consoles — bio-organic interfaces grafted onto the nexus's ancient architecture. Fleshy buttons, tendon-cables, screens displaying the harvesting grid status. These are how the Choir manages the operation from day to day. More familiar technology than the ancient controls.

The universal interface bridges the gap between your capabilities and the Choir's controls. Displays translate to comprehensible data. You can now access the harvesting grid management — redirect siphons, shut down sectors, or...
The bio-organic controls don't respond to your touch — they're keyed to Choir physiology. You need an interface adapter.

objects.name: Ancient Controls
objects.description: Primordial crystalline controls from the Convergence itself.

then.text: Controls older than the planet's civilization — older than most stars. Pure crystal interfaces that respond to energy patterns, not physical touch. These are the Convergence's own controls, from before it enslaved the Choir to do its work. They're incomprehensible.

The core interface module resonates with the ancient controls — it was designed for exactly this. The crystal interfaces light up, responding to the module's energy signature. You now have direct access to the Convergence's own systems. The power is staggering. And dangerous.

objects.name: Harvesting Display
objects.description: Holographic display showing the planet's energy harvesting grid.

then.text: A holographic display showing the planet in real-time. Siphon towers, energy conduits, and the nexus are all highlighted. The planet is nearly 70% drained. At current rates, it has weeks left. The harvesting is accelerating.

objects.name: Spire Interface Terminal
objects.description: The primary control interface for the nexus.

then.text: The primary nexus interface — where harvesting can be managed, redirected, or shut down. Currently locked behind a Convergence-era security system. The lock is crystalline, responding to specific energy patterns.

With the Choir consoles bridged, you can access the spire interface. The full scope of the harvesting operation is now at your fingertips. You could shut it down. Redirect it. Overload it. The choice is yours.

objects.name: Convergence Lock
objects.description: An ancient crystalline security mechanism.

then.text: A crystalline lock mechanism — the Convergence's own security. No keyhole, no code entry. It responds to specific energy patterns. The core interface module might be able to interface with it.
The ancient key resonates with the lock. Crystal patterns align and the mechanism opens, revealing deeper sections of the nexus — including the stasis gallery and the core chamber.

objects.name: Ancient Specimens
objects.description: Beings from billions of years ago, preserved in crystal.

then.text: Dozens of crystal pillars, each containing a perfectly preserved being from a different consumed world. The specimens span billions of years of galactic history — from simple organisms to extraordinarily complex beings. Each one was the last of its kind. This is the Convergence's trophy room.

objects.name: Frozen Inhabitant
objects.description: A four-armed being frozen in crystal, mouth open in a scream.

then.text: One of the planet's former inhabitants — tall, four-armed — frozen in crystal. Their mouth is open in a scream. Their four arms are raised in a gesture of defiance.
